title: Senior Communications Content Strategist
description:
If you’re passionate about building a better future for individuals, communities, and our country—and you’re committed to working hard to play your part in building that future—consider WGU as the next step in your career.

Driven by a mission to expand access to higher education through online, competency-based degree programs, WGU is also committed to being a great place to work for a diverse workforce of student-focused professionals. The university has pioneered a new way to learn in the 21st century, one that has received praise from academic, industry, government, and media leaders. Whatever your role, working for WGU gives you a part to play in helping students graduate, creating a better tomorrow for themselves and their families.

The salary range for this position takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs.

At WGU, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their position, and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is:

Grade: Professional 309

Pay Range: $82,700.00 - $124,000.00

Job Description

The Senior Communications Content Strategist is a member of the Brand Content and Communications team in WGU’s Institutional Advancement (IA) department. This role is responsible for building the university’s reputation among key audiences, including corporate partners, education thought leaders, policy makers, media, alumni, employees, and others.

This role will:

• Strengthen WGU’s brand authority through strategic, compelling storytelling.
• Amplify WGU’s impact by creating, editing, and facilitating content that is outcomes-focused, engaging, and trustworthy.
• Drive measurable channel and audience growth through data-informed and organization-aligned content strategies.

Responsibilities


  • Manage content creation, dissemination, and analytics for the WGU Impact Blog and IgnitED newsletter on LinkedIn.
  • Write, edit, and/or repurpose content for use across WGU’s external channels (e.g., blog to social media, newsletter to short-form video, etc.) as assigned.
  • Execute on the university’s thought leadership strategy, ensuring consistent contributions across channels.
  • Develop and execute distribution strategies across owned, earned and social channels to maximize content reach and engagement.
  • Partner with communications staff regarding communications plans, content topics, copywriting, and editing.
  • Edit and publish press releases and media assets in partnership with communications teams.
  • Create and implement AI-assisted processes to streamline editorial planning, reporting, etc.
  • Optimize content for discoverability across traditional search and AI-driven platforms (e.g. generative search, answer engines), adapting formats and structures as those platforms evolve.
  • Support content development and editing for major university publications and initiatives (commencements, annual reports, etc.) as assigned.
  • Meet personal, team, and department goals in a timely manner.

#LI-BC1

#LI-Onsite

This job description includes a general representation of job requirements rather than a comprehensive inventory of all required responsibilities or work activities. The contents of this document or related job requirements may change at any time with or without notice.


Qualifications


Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities


  • Ability to write insightfully and creatively for various channels and audiences, including blogs, web content, print collateral, etc.. Writing samples or portfolio required.
  • Experience writing for press and media relations purposes, including press releases and media assets.
  • Strong ability to copy, edit and proofread according to both AP and Chicago styles.
  • Experience creating and executing multi-channel communications strategies.
  • Ability to build relationships and manage projects across internal teams.
  • Familiarity with SEO, GEO, and content marketing best practices. Working knowledge of how generative AI and answer engines are shaping content discovery, and ability to adapt content strategy accordingly.
  • Ability to translate one piece of content into multiple channel-native formats to maximize distribution ROI.
  • Ability to create and manage timely, informative channel and content performance reports using tools such as Adobe Analytics, LinkedIn analytics, and similar platforms.
  • Experience with project management tools such as Asana and monday.com.
  • Ability to work independently, prioritize tasks efficiently, and manage projects as assigned.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office.

Education:


  • Bachelor’s degree in English, communications, journalism, public relations, or marketing.



Experience:


  • 5+ years of related experience

Physical Requirements:


  • Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer
  • Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times

Experience in lieu of education:


Equivalent relevant experience performing the essential functions of this job may substitute for education degree requirements. Generally, equivalent relevant experience is defined as 1 year of experience for 1 year of education and is the discretion of the hiring manager.


Preferred Qualifications:


  • Experience in higher education and/or nonprofits
  • Experience with content management systems
  • Experience in data analysis and reporting

Travel:


This position requires occasional travel of up to 20%, including required attendance at designated company summits (typically one to two per year). Additional travel may include conferences, visits to company locations, and other business-related events as needed. Additional travel may be assigned as needed to support business requirements

Position & Application Details

Full-Time Regular Positions (classified as regular and working 40 standard weekly hours): This is a full-time, regular position (classified for 40 standard weekly hours) that is eligible for bonuses; medical, dental, vision, telehealth and mental healthcare; health savings account and flexible spending account; basic and voluntary life insurance; disability coverage; accident, critical illness and hospital indemnity supplemental coverages; legal and identity theft coverage; retirement savings plan; wellbeing program; discounted WGU tuition; and flexible paid time off for rest and relaxation with no need for accrual, flexible paid sick time with no need for accrual, 11 paid holidays, and other paid leaves, including up to 12 weeks of parental leave.

How to Apply: If interested, an application will need to be submitted online. Internal WGU employees will need to apply through the internal job board in Workday.

Additional Information

Disclaimer: The job posting highlights the most critical responsibilities and requirements of the job. It’s not all-inclusive.

Accommodations: Applicants with disabilities who require assistance or accommodation during the application or interview process should contact our Talent Acquisition team at recruiting@wgu.edu.

Equal Employment Opportunity: All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic as required by law.

title: Community Engagement Coordinator
description:
Summary:

Overview:

The Community Engagement Coordinator will work as part of a team to create relationships with key community-based organizations (e.g., human service organizations, animal welfare groups, NYPD & law enforcement agencies) and identify pet owners who would benefit from ASPCA or other services. The Coordinator will participate in field work including visiting clients’ homes to coordinate services as well as transporting animals from veterinary hospitals to the ASPCA hospital and attending community events.


Who We Are:

The ASPCA’s Community Engagement program works in New York City to assist pet owners who need support to care for their animals by addressing underlying systemic issues, such as socioeconomic distress, lack of access to resources, domestic violence, medical or mental health considerations.


What You'll Do:

The Coordinator will partner with community stakeholders and support development of strategic alliances within the community to reach pet owners and increase awareness of the ASPCA’s services, with the goal of keeping more pets healthy and in their homes. This role is responsible for executing engagement plans that incorporates key community members feedback for successful entry of ASPCA services into communities. They will directly connect clients to services and maintain partnership engagement to facilitate better access to services.

  • The Coordinator reports directly to the Senior Manager and has no direct reports.

Where and When You’ll Work

This position reports on-site daily to our Long Island City (Queens) office. The schedule for this role is Sunday-Thursday, 9am - 5pm. This shift is subject to change at the discretion of the ASPCA.


What You’ll Get


Compensation


Starting pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of factors, including but not limited to education, training, experience, location, business needs, internal equity, market demands or budgeted amount for the role. The target hiring range is for new hire offers only, and staff compensation may increase beyond the maximum hiring range based on performance over time. The maximum of the hiring range is reserved for candidates with the highest qualifications and relevant experience. The expected hiring salary range for this role is set forth below and may be modified in the future.

  • The target hiring range for this role is $26.85- $28.29 per hour.

Benefits


At the ASPCA, you don’t have to choose between your passion and making a living. Our comprehensive benefits package helps ensure you can live a rewarding life at work and at home. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • Affordable health coverage, including medical, employer-paid dental and optional vision coverage.
  • Flexible time off that includes vacation time, paid personal time, sick time, bereavement time, paid parental leave, and 10 company paid holidays that allows you even more flexibility to observe the days that mean the most to you.
  • Competitive financial incentives and retirement savings, including a 401(k) plan with generous employer contributions — we match dollar-for-dollar up to 4% and provide an additional 4% contribution toward your future each year.
  • Robust professional development opportunities, including classes, on-the-job training, coaching and mentorship with industry-leading peers, internal mobility, opportunities to support in the field and so much more.

For more information on our benefits offerings, visit our website.

Responsibilities:

Responsibility buckets are listed in general order of importance. They include, but are not limited to:

Program Outreach & Engagement:

  • Participate in events and meetings that promote the ASPCA and NYPD partnership, strengthen relationships with social service partners and benefit the community.

  • Coordinate and lead ASPCA hosted events (vaccine & grooming) 1-2 times per month.

  • Facilitate partnerships with community-based organizations, government agencies and faith-based organizations in New York City and advocate for the integration of pet-related services within existing delivery systems.

  • Build relationships with social service agencies, law enforcement and key government agencies, to generate new cases for the department.

  • Deliver 4-6 trainings per month to community-based organizations, government agencies and law enforcement on the ASPCA’s services, animal welfare and the inclusion of animal issues in human services.

  • Work collaboratively with Senior Manager and Community Engagement team to develop strategic community outreach concepts and execute the planning, coordination and logistics for the events.

  • Collaborate with other ASPCA departments to ensure access to services (for clients) and program goals (for ASPCA programs).

Case Management, Transportation & Field Work:

  • Act as a case lead and provide case management from initiation to completion. Communicate with clients to gather historical information on their pets needs and develop intervention plans that include ASPCA services and referrals to social service agencies when needed. This position will carry 8-10 cases at a time.

  • Transport animals from CE and NYPD cases in the 5 boroughs, and occasionally transport animals to partners in the Northeast.

  • Conduct field visits and develop intervention plans for cases, including frequency of visits and action plans.

  • Provide referrals for mental health, adult protective services, substance abuse and other services as needed.

  • Participate in large scale NYPD and Community Engagement cases that require the physical removal and transport of animals. Assist with daily care (cleaning kennels and habitats, walking and feeding dogs and cats, providing enrichment, doing laundry, etc) for these animals 1-2 times per week for up to 4 weeks on a few occasions per year, with flexibility to extend in certain circumstances)

Special Projects and Professional Development:

  • Serve as the event lead on events that benefit the NYPD partnership (Paws & Police vaccine event, National Night Out, Heroes in Human Services Awards, etc.) as needed

  • Attend (minimum) one local conference/training per year to develop professional goals and promote career growth.

  • Regularly attend ASPCA Voices to cultivate presentation skills.

  • Contribute to department’s monthly newsletter by writing stories on special cases or relevant events.

Qualifications:

  • Strong interpersonal skills

  • Proficient in public speaking

  • Ability to lift up to 40 lbs., stand for long periods and work outside in various conditions

  • Animal handling experience a plus

  • Fluency in Spanish strongly preferred

  • Strong team player, as well as ability to work independently

  • Must provide a valid driver’s license upon hire and pass a motor vehicle history check demonstrating a safe driving history. As part of the driving requirements of this role, must also pass a Department of Transportation Medical Exam

  • Computer literacy with particular proficiency in MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint. Civicore experience a plus

  • Ability to exemplify ASPCA’s core values and behavioral competencies.

Education and Work Experience:

  • High school degree or GED equivalent required

  • 2+ years' experience in community services, community organizing, advocacy or related field required

  • 2+ years' professional experience required

Language:

English (Required), Spanish

Education and Work Experience:

High School Diploma (Required)

Minimum of 2-3 years’ experience in community services, client services, social services, community organizing, advocacy or related field

  • Mentor senior leaders and build strong succession pipelines for critical operations roles.

  • Act as a trusted advisor to the CEO and Board on execution risks, alliance strategy, and scale readiness.
  • Support evaluation of new business models, redevelopment opportunities, and JV proposals from an execution and governance standpoint.

  • Total Experience: 20+ years

title: Assurance Experienced Senior
description:
Job Summary:

The Assurance Experienced Senior will be responsible for coordinating the day-to-day "in-charge" duties of planning, fieldwork, and "wrap-up" to include the preparing of financial statements with disclosures, applying most areas of GAAP as necessary and documenting, validating, testing, and assessing various control systems. This position is also responsible for acting as the client contact for basic questions and information and may be involved in reviews and agreed-upon procedure engagements.


Job Duties:

Control Environment

  • Applies knowledge and understanding of the collective effect of various factors on establishing or enhancing effectiveness, or mitigating the risks, of specific policies and procedures.
  • As Auditor in charge is responsible to the engagement manager for the day-to-day conduct of the audit work and in particular for ensuring that the field work is executed and completed as planned, in accordance with timetable, with Firm’s policies and procedures and to budget
  • Applies knowledge of transactional flow and key transactional cycles to complete audit work
  • Documents, validates, and assesses effectiveness of internal control system
  • Determines and communicates improvements to client internal controls and accounting procedures
  • Supervise the work of audit staff and review workpapers and conclusions and explaining any shortcomings to them

GAAP

  • Applies knowledge and understanding of governing principles; applying these principles to client transactions; and documenting and communicating an understanding and application of these principles.
  • Understand and effectively communicate financial statement disclosure requirements to clients
  • Identifies and applies new pronouncements to client situations
  • Identifies, analyzes, and discusses alternative generally accepted accounting principles for the client, when necessary, with the Manager, Senior Manager and engagement partner
  • Identifies complex accounting issues and brings them to the attention of superiors for resolution

SEC and PCAOB

  • Applies knowledge and understanding of SEC regulations and PCAOB guidelines, and documents and communicates the application of these principles.
  • Reads and reviews clients’ SEC filings, ensuring accuracy and completeness, and also ensuring all financial information is supported in the workpapers and appropriately tested
  • Prepares required communications to the Client and the Audit Committee
  • Plans and executes Section 404 internal control audit including obtaining an understanding of the control environment, designing test plans, evaluating deficiencies, and assessing the overall financial reporting control environment.

GAAS

  • Applies knowledge and understanding of professional standards; application of the principles contained in professional standards; and the ability to document and communicate an understanding and application of professional standards on an engagement.
  • Formulates and communicates the audit plan
  • Applies GAAS to a variety of complex issues and consults others as appropriate
  • Applies of audit skepticism and determines when to reduce or expand testing
  • Uses BDO audit manuals as appropriate for the situation
  • Documents deviations from BDO policy with approval
  • Look for opportunities to suggest improvement to company’s internal controls and prepare draft communication required by professional standards.

Methodology

  • Applies knowledge and application of BDO standards that guide effective and efficient delivery of quality services and products.
  • Applies BDO audit approach and methodologies, including tools and technology, to execute the audit with quality, efficiency, and completeness despite pressures of deadlines
  • Identifies and proposes outcomes to critical issues

Research

  • Applies methodology used to seek or maintain information from authoritative sources and to draw conclusions regarding a target issue based on that information.
  • Applies knowledge of the use of internal and external research tools and selects methodology for routine research requests
  • Researches more complex areas of accounting and forms an initial opinion on the correct treatment independently and considers and documents the impact on the client and audit engagement
  • Documents and organizes complicated findings in a usable format, based on information obtained from Accounting Research Manager, BDO Assurance Manual, Yahoo Finance, etc.
  • Assist the engagement manager with gathering sufficient appropriate information about the business and information system, including the accounting system, to form an adequate basis for the preparation of the audit strategy


Project Management

  • Coordinate timing of planning, fieldwork, and review with audit team and client and assist engagement executives in developing the audit engagement budget and identify appropriate resources.
  • Develop the draft Audit Engagement Planning Memorandum, audit programs and budgets
  • Establish with the engagement manager the responsibilities of individual audit staff for specific areas of audit work
  • Monitor and report engagement budget to actual and advise engagement executives of possible overruns

Other duties as required

Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • Supervise a team of audit professionals ranging in size from 1 to 5
  • Provide verbal and written performance feedback to associates
  • Teach/coach associates to provide on the job learning

Qualifications, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics or Statistics, required OR Bachelor’s degree in other focus area and CPA certification, required Master’s degree in Accountancy, preferred

Experience:

  • Three (3) or more years of prior relevant audit experience and/or public accounting, private industry accounting or consulting/professional services experience, required
  • Prior basic supervisory experience, preferred

License/Certifications:

  • Eligible to sit for the CPA exams upon starting employment, required, and actively pursuing completion of the exams, required
  • CPA, preferred

Software:

  • Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite, preferred
  • Experience with assurance applications and research tools, preferred

Language:

  • N/A

Other Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • Possess proven solid verbal and written communication skills
  • Possess people development and delegation skills
  • Possess executive presence - needs to be able to be primary contact for the client
  • Ability to "in-charge" all stages of the audit, including planning, fieldwork, and "wrap-up"
  • Ability to perform the completion of an audit of a complex company
  • Ability to prepare and/or review financial statements with disclosures in accordance with GAAP requirements.

description:
At Tiffany & Co., joy is central to everything we do, from crafting our exceptional pieces to inspiring clients to express and celebrate the many facets of love. It’s a skill that we’ve been perfecting since 1837, one empowered by our daring vision and entrepreneurial spirit. Together, each generation of employees honor our past while dreaming of our future. We are looking for thoughtful, curious, and optimistic talents, seeking to deliver excellence and to contribute to Tiffany & Co.’s continued legacy.

Overview

The Tiffany Ambassador will deliver the Tiffany Touch to every client they interact with and set the tone for their visit to The Landmark. Ambassadors connect daily with clients, building brand desirability through unique face-to-face interactions and inspiring storytelling. Stationed throughout The Landmark, Tiffany & Co. Ambassadors have a significant influence on the client’s journey and experience within the store. Tiffany & Co. Ambassadors greet and welcome clients as the embodiment of the Tiffany Warm Welcome and hold the critical position of embodying the brand through every client interaction.

Support Client Experience:

  • Welcome all clients in a warm and courteous manner, helping to create an exemplary luxury experience that positively impacts both service and sales.
  • Exhibit passion and instill inspiration using storytelling to share knowledge of the World of Tiffany.
  • Consistently deliver a knowledgeable and curated experience for every client.
  • Attend to the needs of internal and external clients while greeting and directing clients throughout the Landmark ensuring Tiffany expectations are always delivered.
  • Engage in bespoke conversations to elevate the in-store experience and discern client needs, partnering them with the appropriate Client Advisor to achieve sales goals.
  • As dictated by the needs of the business, support all hospitality, tours, and selling events through various means including door coverage, elevator operation, Hospitality support, and BOH support.
  • Accurately manage floor waiting lists and execute efficiencies and best practices to better support in-store experience.
  • Communicate with management any potential service issues in a timely manner.
  • Share client interactions and impressions of the brand with management.
  • Fosters collaboration and works best in a team environment.
  • Support Company Initiatives and demonstrate agility when it comes to change.

Experience

Required:

  • Minimum of 2 years of retail, or luxury retail store experience or relevant client-related experience (e.g., hospitality, museum/art gallery, etc.).
  • Flexibility to work non-traditional hours, including days, nights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Must have authorization to work in the United States

Desired:

  • A college/university degree with a fine or performing arts focus.
  • Gemological Institute of America (GIA) coursework is preferred.
  • The ability to speak multiple languages.

Tiffany & Co. is formed from many facets - talented people who make our community stronger with their creativity, perspective, and lived experience. This is why diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging (DEIB) are at the core of our business and our culture. We’re committed to creating a more inclusive jewelry industry that empowers people of all backgrounds to shine and evolve to new heights.

We believe reaching your full potential requires a solid foundation, and your well-being is a central pillar. Tiffany employees are eligible for comprehensive benefits, including global benefits like adoption and surrogacy assistance, and parental leave, as well as programs that support mental, emotional, physical, and financial well-being. We also offer competitive pay, medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) plans with company match, paid time off, alongside other meaningful employee offerings.

The hiring range for this position ranges from $19.72 - $26.00 per hour. The rate of pay offered will be dependent upon candidates’ relevant skills and experience.

title: Data Engineer
description:
Data Engineer
£45,000 to £55,000 plus great benefits (Work Level 6A)
Manchester city centre - in this role you’ll work in a hybrid way splitting your time between home and the office (find out more about our hybrid working policy at https://jobs.coop.co.uk/hybrid-working-policy).

Please be aware Co-op does not offer visa sponsorship for this opportunity

We’re open to applications from people who may require flexible working arrangements. There’ll be an opportunity to discuss your flexible working requirements during the interview process, and at offer stage.

We’re looking for Data Engineers to join us and help transform the way we do business. We’re building a new data platform in Databricks to improve our data science, analytics, and business intelligence capabilities, and you’ll play a key part in this.

Why this role matters

As a Data Engineer at Co-op, you’ll collaborate with the wider team and use coding languages such as Python and SQL to solve complex data problems and optimise outcomes across our Food Retail, Funeralcare, and Insurance business areas. If you can bring us the passion, curiosity, and problem-solving skills that we’re looking for, we can offer you the opportunity to build your career and provide data solutions that bring value to millions of our colleagues, customers, and member-owners.

What you’ll do

• Collaborate with partners across the wider Co-op to build an understanding of their data problems and design solutions that satisfy business needs
• Develop, build and maintain enterprise data solutions within our cloud data platform, building automation and quality into everything we do
• Hands-on development of data pipelines using technologies and programme languages such as Databricks, PySpark and SQL
• Help to develop and implement our data architecture and engineering roadmap across our data teams

What you’ll bring

We’re committed to making our roles as accessible as possible, so we only ask for the minimum criteria. To thrive here, you’ll need to bring:

• Significant experience working as a Data Engineer and delivering modern data architectures within a multi-disciplinary engineering team(s)
• Experience using coding languages such as Python and SQL
• Excellent organisation, communication, and collaboration skills
• Ability to work in an agile environment and adapt to changing priorities
• Good problem-solving skills, with a natural curiosity for emerging technologies and a desire to explore how these could be used to solve all kinds of complex modern business problems

We know some people may hesitate to apply if they don’t meet every requirement. At Co-op, we’re committed to building diverse and inclusive teams, so if you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t align perfectly, we still encourage you to apply.

Why Co-op?

At Co-op, we’re owned by our members. And because we’re owned by you, we can do right by you. So when you join us, you’re not just taking a job, you’re joining a movement. We’re an organisation that puts people and communities first, and we’re powered by purpose. We want this to be a place where you can thrive, so you’ll also receive:

• An annual bonus (based on personal and business performance)
• 28 days holiday (rising to 32 with service) plus bank holidays
• A pension with up to 10% employer contributions
• Access to a subsidised onsite gym (at our Manchester HQ)
• 30% discount on Co-op products and 10% off other brands
• Stream – early access to a percentage of your pay as you earn it
• Virtual healthcare including GP appointments, mental health support, nutrition and fitness advice
• 24/7 colleague support service
• Training and support for your development and career progression
• Cycle-to-work scheme

A place you’ll belong

We’re building diverse and inclusive teams that reflect the communities we serve. We welcome applications from everyone and are committed to creating a workplace where colleagues can feel like they belong, supported by our inclusive policies and the ways we work.

We’re proud to be part of the Disability Confident scheme and offer interviews to disabled candidates who meet the minimum criteria for a job. If you need any adjustments during the recruitment process, we’ll support you.

Learn more about our recruitment process at jobs.coop.co.uk/apply-process and our inclusion commitments at jobs.coop.co.uk/diversity-inclusion

Please note that we may close applications for this role early.

title: Resourcing Specialist
description:
Job Title: Resourcing Specialist - Cybersecurity

Location: UK or EU

Job type: Full-Time Permanent



About us:


Integrity360 is a leading independent cybersecurity and PCI specialist operating across Europe, Africa, the Caribbean, and North America. The company has office locations in Ireland, the UK, Bulgaria, Italy, Sweden, Spain, Lithuania, Ukraine, Africa, the Caribbean, and Canada, supported by eight Security Operations Centres (SOCs) located in Dublin, Sofia, Madrid, Stockholm, Paris, Rome, Johannesburg and Cape Town.

With over 900 employees, including more than 600 dedicated cybersecurity professionals, Integrity360 delivers a full suite of professional, support, and managed security services. These span the complete cyber risk lifecycle, from identification and prevention to detection, response, and recovery. Integrity360 supports over 3000 mid-market and enterprise organisations across sectors including financial services, insurance, government, healthcare, retail, telecommunications, and utilities.


At Integrity360, people come first. We invest heavily in learning, development and progression, fostering a dynamic culture where innovation, collaboration and continuous growth are at the heart of what we do. If you're ready to take your cyber security career to the next level, we’d love to hear from you.



The opportunity:



At Integrity360, our people and their expertise are central to the services we deliver. We are looking for a commercially minded and highly organised Professional Services Resource Planning Specialist to help us match the right skills and capacity to customer demand.


You will sit at the heart of our Professional Services operation, working closely with delivery leaders, project managers, sales and finance. Through effective resource planning, reporting and stakeholder coordination, you will help us improve utilisation, support revenue delivery and provide greater visibility of capacity and future demand.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who enjoys bringing structure to a fast-moving environment, working with data and collaborating across multiple teams and regions.



What you will do:



  • Coordinate the allocation of Professional Services consultants across customer projects and internal initiatives.
  • Maintain an accurate view of consultant capacity, availability, skills and planned assignments.
  • Work with delivery leaders and project managers to anticipate resource requirements and resolve scheduling conflicts.
  • Partner with sales and delivery teams to understand upcoming demand across the pipeline and backlog.
  • Identify available capacity and connect relevant skills with upcoming customer opportunities.
  • Monitor utilisation and highlight emerging risks, gaps and opportunities.
  • Produce clear, accurate reporting on capacity, utilisation, backlog, pipeline and resource demand.
  • Support revenue forecasting and accrual processes by working closely with Professional Services and finance teams.
  • Monitor time-recording compliance and help resolve missing or inaccurate submissions.
  • Maintain reliable resource planning data across relevant systems and reporting tools.
  • Support workforce planning by identifying skills gaps, recruitment requirements and potential subcontractor needs.
  • Recommend improvements to resource planning processes, reporting and operational ways of working.



What you will bring:



  • Experience in resource planning, workforce planning, Professional Services operations, PMO, project coordination or a similar environment.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Confidence working with data and translating it into clear, practical insight.
  • Advanced or strong working knowledge of Microsoft Excel.
  • Experience with Power BI, resource management platforms, PSA tools or project management systems would be beneficial.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Commercial awareness, with an understanding of utilisation, capacity, revenue, pipeline or project-based delivery.
  • A proactive and solutions-focused approach.
  • High attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining accurate information.
  • The ability to work effectively with colleagues across different teams, disciplines and geographical regions.
  • Experience within cybersecurity, technology, consulting or another Professional Services environment would be advantageous, but it does not need to be mandatory.



What success looks like:



In this role, success means:

  • Delivery teams have a reliable view of capacity and availability.
  • Consultants are assigned to work that aligns with their skills and experience.
  • Resource conflicts and delivery risks are identified early.
  • Leadership has clear insight into utilisation, demand and skills gaps.
  • Sales, delivery and finance work from consistent and accurate information.
    Available capacity is proactively connected with customer demand.



Why join Integrity360?



Integrity360 provides an opportunity to build your career within a growing cybersecurity organisation operating across multiple regions.


You will work with talented colleagues across Professional Services, project management, sales and finance, while gaining broad exposure to how a modern cybersecurity services business operates. You will have the opportunity to improve processes, influence decision-making and make a visible contribution to the performance and growth of the business.


We value collaboration, accountability, continuous learning and new ideas. You will be encouraged to bring your experience, challenge existing ways of working and help us build a more scalable and data-led resource planning capability.

title: Captive Consulting Team Leader
description:
The Manager, Captive Consulting leads the firm’s captive consulting practice as a people leader, directing engagement delivery, colleague development, and growth of the practice. As a senior strategic advisor, the Manager serves the firm’s most significant and most complex captive relationships, guiding feasibility studies, formation projects, and ongoing program reviews. This leader partners with practice and firm leadership to expand capabilities, shape practice strategy, and drive new business across the captive insurance market. The role combines deep captive and alternative risk financing expertise with proven people leadership and business development.

Position Summary


The Manager, Captive Consulting leads the firm’s captive consulting practice as a people leader, directing engagement delivery, colleague development, and growth of the practice. As a senior strategic advisor, the Manager serves the firm’s most significant and most complex captive relationships, guiding feasibility studies, formation projects, and ongoing program reviews. This leader partners with practice and firm leadership to expand capabilities, shape practice strategy, and drive new business across the captive insurance market. The role combines deep captive and alternative risk financing expertise with proven people leadership and business development.


Primary Responsibilities


Team Leadership & Development


· Leads, mentors, and develops a team of Captive Consultants and Senior Captive Consultants, overseeing staffing, workload, quality, and professional development.

· Establishes and maintains quality and methodology standards for feasibility studies and other captive deliverables across the team’s book of business.


Client & Advisory


· Serves as senior strategic advisor for the firm’s largest and most complex captive client relationships.

· Oversees delivery of feasibility studies, formation projects, and ongoing captive program reviews across the practice.


Practice Growth & Market Leadership


· Drives growth of the captive consulting practice by identifying new business opportunities, leading proposals and responses to requests for proposal, and representing the practice in industry associations and events.

· Builds and maintains relationships with captive domicile regulators, captive managers, actuaries, and other third-party providers.

· Represents the practice in thought leadership, speaking engagements, and marketing materials.


Practice Operations & Strategy


· Partners with firm leadership on resourcing, budget, and strategic priorities for the captive consulting practice.

· Monitors industry, regulatory, and tax developments affecting captive insurance and adjusts practice strategy accordingly.

· Performs other duties as assigned.


Required Knowledge & Experience


· Deep expertise in captive structures, domiciles, feasibility analysis, and regulatory and tax considerations.

· Strong knowledge of alternative risk financing and the broader risk management landscape.

· Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent client engagements while driving practice growth.

· Executive-level communication and presentation skills, including experience advising senior client and firm stakeholders.

· Demonstrated success in business development and in building client and industry relationships.

· Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook) and relevant analytical and engagement management tools.


Qualifications


· Bachelor’s degree required; an advanced degree is a plus.

· 5–7 years of relevant experience in captive consulting, risk management, or alternative risk financing, including experience leading teams.

· Relevant industry designations (e.g., ARM, CPCU, CCM, or similar) preferred.

· Travel may be required to client sites, captive domiciles, and industry events.


Skills & Behaviors


Functional/Technical Skills


· Risk Financing & Alternative Risk Transfer: Structures and advises on captive and alternative risk financing solutions, from feasibility through formation and ongoing optimization.

· Specialty Lines Product Knowledge: Applies deep knowledge of captive structures, domiciles, and specialty coverage to the firm’s most complex programs.

· Complex Account Strategy: Sets strategic direction for the firm’s largest and most complex captive relationships, aligning program design to client objectives.

· Regulatory Affairs & Licensing: Navigates captive domicile regulatory and tax requirements and maintains strong relationships with regulators and third-party providers.

· Proposal Development & RFP Response: Leads proposals and competitive pursuits that grow the captive consulting practice.

· Executive Communication: Advises senior client and firm leaders and represents the practice in thought leadership and speaking engagements.

Behaviors


· Strategic Influence: Shapes practice strategy and influences client and firm leadership on complex captive decisions.

· Client Focus: Anticipates and serves the needs of the firm’s most significant captive relationships.

title: Payment Anomaly Detection Lead Business Analyst - Assistant Vice President
description:
Who we are looking for:

We are looking for an experienced payments business analyst and control specialist to lead the business delivery of the Payment Anomaly Detection capability. During implementation, the role will be responsible for business requirements, rule and process design, data validation, user story development, testing, governance, and operational readiness. Following go-live, the role will transition into a senior operations leadership position responsible for the ongoing management of the capability, including operational oversight, business-owned rule management & governance, performance management, issue resolution, control effectiveness, and continuous enhancement of the anomaly detection framework


Why this role is important to us?

The anomaly detection capability will operate to identify unusual payments while protecting straight-through processing and payment cut-offs. Strong business ownership is required to ensure rules are explainable, tested, governed and supported by an effective exception-management operating model.

Join us if contributing to our Payments Business Risk and Resiliency Programs is a challenge you are up for.


What you will be responsible for

  • Lead business analysis for the anomaly detection workstream, translating the BRD into detailed requirements, user stories, process flows and acceptance criteria.
  • Own the business rules catalogue and coordinate the definition, documentation and prioritisation of customer, corridor, currency, rail, amount, time-of-day and cut-off-aware rules.
  • Validate data inputs, historical baselines, payment identifiers, lifecycle attributes, entitlements, reference data and calculation logic used by rules and model outputs.
  • Lead business review of UI, queue, filtering, tab management, case management, client-contact, explainability, dashboard and audit-trail functionality.
  • Design controlled rule-change governance, including role-based access, maker-checker approval, rationale capture, versioning, effective dates, rollback and segregation of duties.
  • Coordinate scenario design, test data, system integration testing, user acceptance testing, regression testing, defect triage and evidence sign-off.
  • Define operational playbooks for false positives, high-risk anomalies, mandatory holds, client validation, missed cut-offs, high-volume events and approved resilience scenarios.
  • Prepare and manage the BAU operating model, including queue ownership, escalation routes, procedures, training, coverage, capacity, KPIs, KRIs and governance forums.
  • After go-live, oversee operations, rule effectiveness, false positives, alert volumes, override trends, drift indicators and tuning recommendations within approved governance.
  • Align anomaly detection and cyber-response processes so suspicious or incorrect payment activity is triaged effectively during resilience events.
  • Provide senior operational support during incidents, high-volume alert events and material rule or control changes.

What we value:

These skills will help you succeed in this role:

  • Strong payments business analysis experience with the ability to translate control objectives into implementable requirements.
  • Knowledge of payment operations, SWIFT or ISO 20022 messages, payment rails, cut-offs, sanctions screening, fraud or anomaly controls.
  • Experience in rule design, data analysis, process mapping, testing, defect management and operational readiness.
  • Strong control mindset with practical knowledge of RBAC, maker-checker, audit evidence and segregation of duties.
  • Ability to lead workshops and influence Technology, Analytics, Risk, Compliance and Operations stakeholders.

Education & Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, data, technology or a related discipline.
  • 7+ years of financial services experience, preferably in payments, controls, fraud, screening or change delivery.

title: Quality Assurance Technician- Widmer Brothers Brewery
description:
About Tilray Brands, Inc.

Tilray Brands, Inc. (“Tilray”) (Nasdaq: TLRY; TSX: TLRY), is leading global lifestyle and consumer packaged goods company with operations in Canada, the United States, Europe, Australia, and Latin America that is leading as a transformative force at the nexus of cannabis, beverage, wellness, and entertainment, elevating lives through moments of connection. Tilray’s mission is to be a leading premium lifestyle company with a house of brands and innovative products that inspire joy, wellness and create memorable experiences. Tilray’s unprecedented platform supports over 40 brands in over 20 countries, including comprehensive cannabis offerings, hemp-based foods, and craft beverages.


OUR MISSION:

Back in ’79 it was tough for brothers Kurt and Rob Widmer to find beer that they enjoyed to drink. So, they took it into their own hands and began home brewing for themselves and their friends. Kurt and Rob decided to do what most people only dream of: quit their jobs and turn their beer hobby into a vocation. So, they scrounged up equipment from wherever they could, including a dairy tank turned mash tun, a shrimp cooker turned whirlpool and a 1970 Datsun pickup truck “borrowed” from their dad. Cobbling it all together, they built the Widmer Brewing Company in an industrial part of NW Portland, what is now the Pearl District.

In 1986 the Widmer Brothers created the first American-style Hefeweizen or Hefe, which is translated from German as ‘yeast wheat’. If you ever run into the Widmer Brothers, make sure you pronounce their beloved beer as they intended, “hey-fuh”.

Today Hefeweizen is Oregon’s favorite craft beer and continues to win awards at national beer festivals including a Bronze at The Great American Beer Festival. The Widmer Brothers Brewery continues to crank out new beers and is the leader in Oregon’s innovative craft beer scene.

ROLE SUMMARY:


Ever taken a slug of delicious beer and thought to yourself, "dang this is good, I wish I could work at a brewery!"? Now is your chance!

Whether you are looking to kickstart a career in beer or already have some experience, we are excited for you to apply. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, rewarding workplace and professional growth opportunities.

Our Widmer Brothers Portland Brewery is looking for a QA Tech to join our team! As a QA Tech, you will perform various studies and statistical analysis to improve quality throughout the brewery. You will also run routine analyses of packaged beer for oxygen, carbon dioxide, fill level, etc. .


Job Responsibilities

  • Support the Widmer Brother’s Company's Vision, Mission and Values
  • Perform necessary quality assurance testing (e.g. daily beer checks, measurements on packaging materials, beer chemistry, beer carbon dioxide and air levels, label and finished package quality, etc).
  • Perform necessary microbiological testing, recording, and reporting.
  • Identify problem areas and contribute to the problem solving process working with brewing and maintenance.
  • Maintain the lab in a neat and orderly condition and ensure a sufficient supply of consumable materials.
  • Participate in ongoing product and process improvement efforts.
  • Run routine analyses on packaging materials and beer involved in being packaged.
  • Sample collection at various points during process.
  • A willingness to learn and become part of a small team.
  • Be a team player focused on meeting production, quality, and safety goals.
  • Perform project work as needed.
  • Ability to work and communicate with all levels of Production personnel.
  • Willing to work in a Production facility and collect samples throughout the process.
  • Laboratory testing in microbiology & beer chemistry

Qualifications


  • BA/BS in one of the natural sciences. Microbiology, Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology or Food Sciences is required.
  • Experience in QC/QA in the beverage industry a plus; Production food laboratory experience in QC/QA or R&D desired.
  • Sensory panel training and experience is a plus.
  • Packaging experience is a plus.
  • Familiar with laboratory instrumentation.
  • Experience working with high speed filler, high speed labeler and other packaging line equipment is ideal.
  • Understanding of the brewing process a plus.
  • Excellent communication skills.
  • Possess the stamina for continuous standing and walking.
  • Ability to work 12 hour shifts on a rotating schedule (days and night shifts).
  • Ability to lift 50 lbs.

title: Senior Director, IT Service Operations
description:
Summary:

Overview

The Senior Director, IT Service Operations owns the IT Service Operations pillar: Technical Support, Networks, Asset and Fleet Management, Account Management and identity provisioning, and Service Delivery. This role is the operational command layer that translates strategy into daily execution, holds the pillar accountable to published standards, and builds the operating model that lets managers manage and engineers engineer without constant escalation. This is a people leadership and operational management role, not a technical architect or engineer role. You will set the standards, evaluate work against them, and hold engineers accountable to them. Success is measured by the performance, cohesion, and growth of the team, and by the maturity of the practices the team runs.


Who We Are

The ASPCA is the nation's largest humane society and one of the world's leading animal welfare organizations. Our mission is to provide effective means for the prevention of cruelty to animals throughout the United States. The Information Technology division supports approximately 1,400 employees across New York City headquarters, shelters, clinics, mobile rescue units, and field operations nationwide.

This is an opportunity to lead a transformation as the pillar is in active growth and we are looking for someone to establish practices where none exist, retire workarounds that have become load-bearing, and shepherd a shift toward structured, repeatable operations through coaching and collaboration rather than mandate. The candidate who will thrive here wants to build, is energized by ambiguity and challenge, and is driven by our mission.

A cover letter is optional, but strongly encouraged.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead the IT service operations that keep animal welfare work moving, across shelters, clinics, mobile rescue units, and field operations nationwide. As Sr. Director, IT Service Operations, you will build the operating model, standards, and team capability that carry the ASPCA's technology organization from reactive support to disciplined, measurable service delivery for more than 1,400 staff.

  • The Sr. Director, IT Service Operations reports directly to the VP, Technology Services and has 4-6 direct and matrixed reports, with approximately 15 indirect reports. Additionally, this role serves as the operational deputy to the VP, Technology Services, acting with delegated authority during the VP's absence and at the VP's direction on matters that extend across the division.

Where and When You’ll Work

  • This is a hybrid position requiring a minimum of 2 days per week on-site at an ASPCA New York City area location, with additional travel to ASPCA sites as described below.
  • Ability and willingness to travel up to 15% annually to ASPCA shelter, clinic, and field sites, as needed. Travel may involve environments with animals and standard shelter or clinic conditions
  • Must be available for off-hours escalation and major incident bridge participation, and shares the after-hours escalation rotation with the IT Leadership

What You’ll Get

Compensation

Starting pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of factors, including but not limited to education, training, experience, location, business needs, internal equity, market demands or budgeted amount for the role. The target hiring range is for new hire offers only, and staff compensation may increase beyond the maximum hiring range based on performance over time. The maximum of the hiring range is reserved for candidates with the highest qualifications and relevant experience. The expected hiring salary range for this role is set forth below and may be modified in the future.

· The target hiring range for this role is $188,000 - $200,000 annually

Benefits

At the ASPCA, you don’t have to choose between your passion and making a living. Our comprehensive benefits package helps ensure you can live a rewarding life at work and at home. Our benefits include but are not limited to:

  • Affordable health coverage, including medical, employer-paid dental and optional vision coverage.
  • Flexible time off that includes vacation time, paid personal time, sick time, bereavement time, paid parental leave, and 10 company paid holidays that allows you even more flexibility to observe the days that mean the most to you.
  • Competitive financial incentives and retirement savings, including a 401(k) plan with generous employer contributions — we match dollar-for-dollar up to 4% and provide an additional 4% contribution toward your future each year.
  • Robust professional development opportunities including classes, on-the-job training, coaching and mentorship with industry-leading peers, internal mobility, opportunities to support in the field and so much more.

Responsibilities:

Responsibilities

Responsibility buckets are listed in general order of importance. They include, but are not limited to:

People Leadership and Team Development:

  • Manage a team of 4-6 employees to succeed in their role by communicating clear expectations, providing opportunities for learning and development and building positive and trusting relationships.
  • Support your direct reports by holding regular effective feedback conversations, career conversations, annual performance evaluations and ongoing check-in conversations with each team member on a cadence that's appropriate for their role(s).
  • Translate the VP's strategy into documented team-level goals and measurable quarterly deliverables for each function in the pillar, and review progress against them on a published cadence.
  • Produce and maintain cross-training and succession coverage plans that eliminate single points of failure across Technical Support, Networks, Asset Management, and Account Management.
  • Develop strategic planning capability in senior individual contributors, creating pathways for functional experts to own roadmaps and standards rather than only deliverables.
  • Own recruitment and onboarding for open positions within the pillar, partnering with Talent Acquisition to close gaps that constrain service coverage.
  • Serve as the primary escalation path for functional managers, resolving complexity and assigning resources so that the need for escalation is a rarity.
  • Partner with the VP and People Team on performance management, including documentation and follow-through.

Infrastructure Service Operations and Daily Execution:

  • Own the daily and weekly operating rhythm across all supported locations, including standups, incident triage, change windows, and escalation management.
  • Oversee multi-site technical operations across New York City, Ohio, Florida, Los Angeles, Illinois, North Carolina, and other field locations, ensuring service continuity and site-specific coverage plans.
  • Own on-call rotation coverage and its long-term sustainability, monitoring load distribution and rotation health as a leading indicator of team wellbeing.
  • Serve as the operational deputy to the VP, Technology Services, stepping in with delegated authority during the VP's absence and at the VP's direction on matters that extend across the division, including cross-pillar escalations and time-sensitive decisions that cannot wait for the VP's return.
  • Own scheduled disaster recovery and service continuity testing for services within the pillar, and document results and remediation.
  • Lead major incident response including bridge ownership, stakeholder communication, root cause analysis coordination, and post-incident review facilitation.
  • Share the after-hours major incident escalation rotation with IT Leadership.
  • Maintain the pillar's resource allocation model and surface demand versus capacity gaps before they become delivery failures.
  • Own the outcomes of network engineering strategy across all ASPCA locations. Set the multi-site network roadmap, hold architecture and resilience standards including ISP redundancy and carrier diversity, and negotiate framework decisions with departmental stakeholders to reach the best organizational outcome rather than the fastest local one.
  • Partner with the Sr. Network Engineer as the operational owner of network delivery, incorporating site-level operating expertise into strategy formation while developing their strategic planning capability toward broader ownership over time.

ITSM Practice Ownership and Process Maturity:

  • Own the ITIL practice set for the pillar covering Incident, Problem, Change Enablement, Service Request, and Knowledge Management. Publish and enforce the operating standards for each, including severity classification, escalation paths, SLA and OLA definitions, and major incident runbooks, and advance the pillar from informal practice to documented, repeatable, and measured operations.
  • Define and publish the pillar's performance measurement system. Select the metric set, build the FreshService reporting infrastructure that produces it, and report results in quarterly operational reviews with the VP and functional managers.
  • Chair the existing Change Advisory Board and hold teams accountable to change management standards, including a defined exception path for emergency change.
  • Own the Problem Management practice and the Known Error Database, ensuring problem records close only with documented remediation or formally accepted risk.
  • Own support scale transformation as a practice under ITSM services, covering knowledge management, self-service, and onboarding and offboarding service design, measured against published deflection and time-to-productive targets.
  • Own the FreshService governance model including service catalog structure, knowledge article standards, assignment group configuration, and reporting dashboards, partnering with the Sr. Manager, Technical Services as platform owner.
  • Own the runbook program: define the standard, assign ownership to functional engineers, and track completion against quarterly targets.

Identity, Access, and Asset Lifecycle:

  • Define and implement the joiner-mover-leaver operational SLA and establish mean time to revoke access as a tracked and reported metric.
  • Own role-based access control design and rollout across services within the pillar.
  • Serve as the pillar's operational lead in the enterprise identity and access management program, partnering with the identity provisioning function and the security team.
  • Own asset life cycle end to end, from procurement and provisioning through refresh and secure disposal.
  • Establish and maintain the authoritative system of record for IT asset and configuration data, retiring shadow inventories in favor of a single source of truth

Governance, Security Partnership, and Financial Accountability:

  • Own the pillar's operating budget, tracking spend, forecasting hardware refresh and license true-ups, and partnering with program and department leaders on forecasts for the services their teams consume.
  • Own the pillar's standards library including configuration baselines, endpoint compliance targets, and operational runbooks.
  • Serve as matrixed co-owner of Enterprise Application Management governance covering Box, Microsoft 365, and Okta administration standards, partnering with the Cloud Architect and Information Security Analyst until a dedicated Enterprise Applications Administrator is in place.
  • Partner with the Information Security function on access reviews, endpoint compliance baselines, privileged deprovisioning execution, and evidence collection for security control frameworks including CIS Controls IG1.
  • Build feedback loops between support, infrastructure, and endpoint teams to surface systemic issues before they become incidents.
  • Represent the IT Service Operations pillar in cross-functional forums with peer IT pillars and program stakeholders.

Vendor and Partner Oversight:

  • Own day-to-day operational accountability for the managed service provider, SOC, and NOC engagement, covering SLA compliance review, escalation handling, and monthly service reviews.
  • Serve as operational liaison to the identity and access management implementation partner, ensuring deliverables are actioned within the pillar.
  • Surface vendor contract performance deviations to the VP before they require renegotiation or formal escalation.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Strong people leader, able to manage managers or senior individual contributors across multiple sites, including remote workers in various time zones
  • Familiarity with chairing a change advisory board and driving adoption across teams accustomed to working informally
  • Strong systems thinking, tracing recurring incidents and service failures to structural root causes, including organizational and process causes, rather than treating symptoms
  • Proficiency with an ITSM platform such as FreshService or equivalent, including service catalog design, knowledge article standards, assignment group configuration, and reporting preferred
  • Proficiency making effective use of AI-assisted tools, validating output with sound engineering judgment
  • Demonstrated commitment to animal welfare, or to a comparable mission, and the judgment to weigh technology decisions against mission impact rather than technical elegance alone
  • Creates specific and practical implementation steps from broad or ambiguous transformational goals, and clarifies situations where instructions or objectives are unclear rather than waiting for direction
  • Establishes the standard where none exists rather than escalating for permission, moving quickly on reversible decisions and carefully on irreversible ones
  • Uses a systems approach to think through interdependencies, anticipating consequences and risks across teams and departments before deciding
  • Roots out roadblocks in processes, systems, or practices that inhibit responsiveness, and challenges conventional thinking rather than routing around it
  • Crafts messages that convey the what, why, and how, driving alignment across program, security, and finance stakeholders who do not share a technical vocabulary
  • Recognizes the potential impact of own words and actions due to title or status, and adjusts approach for the audience without changing the message
  • Frames problems so that others can reach root cause themselves, using coaching and discovery rather than directive answers
  • Accepts a high level of accountability for the pillar's performance, results, and budget, and communicates trade-offs on resource decisions rather than absorbing them silently
  • Recognizes the human element of processing change, and helps the team find durable footing during sustained transformation
  • Distinguishes legitimate objection from resistance to change, and builds adoption through coaching rather than mandate
  • Must be available for off-hours escalation and major incident
  • Ability to exemplify ASPCA's core values and behavioral competencies
  • Platform credibility in at least three of the following at a depth sufficient to set the standard and evaluate engineers' work (Preferred): enterprise application administration (such as Microsoft 365, Box, Okta or equivalents); role-based access control design; Zero Touch imaging and Autopilot provisioning; Intune (or equivalent) and mobile device management strategy and execution; enterprise change management; endpoint configuration and compliance baselines
  • Measurable ITIL or ITSM maturity gains delivered in a prior role required
  • Advanced ITIL modules/certifications preferred
  • Must be able to occasionally lift and carry up to 25 lbs. to move IT equipment during site visits and deployments

Language

  • English (required)

Education and Work Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience required
  • 6+ years of progressive IT operations experience required
  • 2+ years managing managers or senior individual contributors within a formal team-lead structure required
  • Experience managing multi-site or geographically distributed technical operations serving frontline staff in field, clinical, or shared-device environments, including on-call and major incident coverage models preferred
  • Experience overseeing outsourced managed service provider, NOC, SOC, or support engagements including SLA governance preferred
  • Experience with asset and configuration management practice, including establishing an authoritative system of record preferred
  • Experience implementing IT Operations components of CIS Controls or an equivalent such as SOC 2 Type 2 or ISO/IEC 27001 preferred
  • Experience establishing ITSM practices where none previously existed, or maturing informal ITSM practice into documented, repeatable, and measured operations required; remaining at the organization to operate these practices for at least two years preferred
  • undefined

  • Experience building portions of a compliance program or leading a first-time implementation or post-failure mediation a plus
  • Experience in a nonprofit, healthcare, or other mission-driven multi-site operating environment preferred

title: Fault Engineer
description:
Who are we?

Ogi is on a mission to power up life online for homes, businesses and communities across South Wales, installing real fibre right up to your doorstep.

In October 2020, we secured landmark multi-million-pound funding to deliver a large-scale and ambitious rollout of full fibre broadband across South Wales.

We believe that joining Ogi is a unique opportunity to work within an innovative Welsh business and one of the fastest-growing companies in Wales. Until now, the pace of levelling up Wales’s broadband infrastructure has been too slow - So we plan to speed things up.

This is a unique opportunity to join an innovative company in a fast-growing sector and help our talented team build a leading Welsh tech business - one that will make a crucial difference to the people and places we serve.

What are we looking for?

We are looking for an experienced and customer-focused Fault Engineer to join our growing Network Operations team.

This is an exciting opportunity for an engineer with a strong background in telecommunications installations, fibre engineering, and fault resolution to play a key role in maintaining and enhancing the performance of our full fibre network.

As a Fault Engineer, you will be responsible for diagnosing and resolving FTTP service issues at customer premises, supporting both residential and business customers. You will combine technical expertise with excellent customer service, taking ownership of faults through to resolution while ensuring the highest standards of quality and professionalism.

The role covers the whole of South Wales, and successful candidates should be comfortable travelling throughout the region to support customers and network operations.

Working closely with the Field Network Engineering Team, NOC and Provisioning teams, you will contribute to maintaining service excellence while developing your knowledge of network operations within one of Wales' fastest-growing fibre providers.

The successful candidate will be safety-conscious, detail-oriented and committed to delivering an exceptional customer experience.


Main responsibilities



Fault Diagnosis & Resolution

• Attend customer premises to investigate and resolve single-user FTTP faults.

• Support SLA performance for residential and business customers.

• Diagnose issues with ONTs, routers, internal wiring, internal fibre drops and customer-owned equipment.

• Test and verify optical power levels, fibre continuity and service performance using approved tools.

• Identify whether faults are internal, external or network-related and take the appropriate escalation actions.

Customer Interaction

• Communicate clearly with customers to understand service issues.

• Explain root causes and resolution steps in a clear and simple manner.

• Provide guidance on in-home connectivity and Wi-Fi optimisation.

Network Integrity & Compliance

• Ensure all work complies with company standards and health & safety procedures.

• Accurately record job outcomes, test results and engineering notes using Dynamics Field Service.

• Escalate persistent or complex faults when required.

Equipment & Installation

• Replace or reinstall customer equipment as required.

• Complete internal fibre repair, re-termination and tidy-up work when necessary.

title: Sr. VIR Technologist
description:
Department/Unit:

Vascular Radiology

Work Shift:

Day (United States of America)

Salary Range:

$84,783.00 - $131,414.00

The Sr. VIR Technologist, under the direction of the Medical Director, the manager, and the physicians, has a key role in providing quality care to patients requiring a wide variety of procedural services. The Sr. VIR Technologist works collaboratively with all members of the team to create diagnostic images, engage in hands-on participation as a procedural assistant, and develop relationships with staff and patients to provide everyone with a safe and positive experience. VIR technologists practice and enforce the radiation safety measures in New York State Department of health code part 16 and support teaching and continued learning for themselves and others as technology evolves.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • PATIENT CARE
    • Educate patients in the purpose and type of test or procedure being performed.
    • Demonstrate the knowledge and skills necessary to provide patient care appropriate to the age and special characteristics of the patient.
    • Review the medical history of a patient (including medications, allergies, lab values, etc.) prior to starting a procedure.
    • Confirm that informed consent has been obtained before starting a procedure.
    • Demonstrate good customer service skills and provide quality care.
    • On call responsibilities with a 30 minute response time after initial contact for 3 services (Neuro, CCP, and Vascular surgery)
  • PROCEDURAL ASSISTANCE
    • Verify that an order for a procedure has been obtained.
    • Set up and maintain a sterile tray and sterile environment appropriate for performance of procedures. The VIR tech
    • Administer contrast media with appropriate application of technical and positioning protocols.
    • Possess, use, and maintain knowledge of radiation protection and safety (ALARA guidelines).
    • Direct and perform a sterile prep of patients for various procedures
    • Assist physicians in all aspects of complex procedures in their assigned area (sterile scrub).
  • EQUIPMENT MAINTENANCE
    • Maintain equipment as needed for a safe and accurate technical function and patient comfort and convenience (including cleaning equipment).
    • Refer equipment problems to the appropriate personnel for service (clinical engineering, etc.).
    • Enter patient data, charges, and supplies into the system accurately.
    • Assist in stocking adequate supply quantities in procedure rooms and rotate for daily use.
    • Actively support AMCH and the imaging department in maintaining proper accreditations.
  • GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES
    • Practice in compliance with Hospital/department policy as well as New York state and accrediting agency standards.
    • Rely on experience and judgement to plan and accomplish goals.
    • Act as a mentor and preceptor to new staff and students.
    • Strives to grow and develop, creating a professional, progressive Imaging department with a positive atmosphere.
    • Involvement in research procedures/protocols.
    • Other duties may be assigned.


Qualifications

  • Associate's Degree Applied Science Degree - required
  • Graduate of an approved professional academic imaging program - required
  • 3+ years experience
  • Demonstrate knowledge of the operation of all IR and OR hybrid procedure rooms. AMC has 5 IR rooms along with a hybrid OR room. Two of the rooms are bi-plane for neuro intervention cases. The procedure rooms at AMC are manufactured by three different companies (Phillips, GE, Siemens), and the VIR techs have to understand the operation of all rooms.
  • Demonstrate knowledge about and proficiency using each of the supplies used for the variety of IR procedures (>900 inventory items and >300 non-stock inventory items). VIR techs also have to be knowledgeable with the supplies used in the OR for AAA repair and bypass procedures (stent grafts).
  • Knowledge of the compatibility of each supply to ensure patient safety. Knowledge of complex cases including but not limited to the treatment of peripheral arterial disease (angiography, stent placement, Atherectomy), portal hypertension (transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunts - TIPS), cancer (Y-90 administration, chemoembolization, port placement), DVT and PE (thrombolysis, thrombectomy), trauma (embolization), aortic aneurysms (endograft placement and revision), dialysis interventions (fistulagrams, angioplasty, declotting, catheter placement), and neurointervention (stroke revascularization, aneurysm and AVM embolization).
  • Communicates cooperatively and effectively to patients, family members, employees and others.
  • Engages in interactive dialogues with the multidisciplinary team.
  • Seek out the input of others to achieve consensus. Reads and interprets documents such as safety rules and procedure manuals.
  • Documents patient care on established forms.
  • Problem-solves, performs exams, and interprets data.
  • Communicates cooperatively and effectively to patients, family members, employees and others.
  • Ability to be honest, to be punctual, and to perform the job in adherence to the highest standards of ethical conduct as defined by AMC and the tenets of the profession.
  • Ability to be accurate in such matters as data entry, exam documentation, and to use good judgment when performing the functions of the job or when interacting with others.
  • Ability to accept direction, carry out orders, to work cooperatively with others and to avoid the creation of unnecessary conflict.
  • Ability to adhere to AMC’s policies, procedures and practices, and to utilize AMC’s problem-solving processes for resolving grievances or disagreements.
  • Ability to anticipate and resolve potential problems to ensure the continuity of appropriate patient care.
  • Ability to identify problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions
  • Ability to improve job performance through continuing education.
  • Relies on experience and judgment to plan and accomplish daily workload.
