I. JOB PURPOSE

Supports Strategic Plan Operations by providing analysis, reporting, and operational coordination that enable program and portfolio-level visibility of Strategic Plan implementation across the organization. Collects, validates, analyzes, and consolidates implementation information to identify trends, dependencies, risks, and implementation considerations, and develops insights that support planning, issue escalation, governance inputs, and leadership decision-making.


II. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Analyzes, synthesizes, and interprets strategic plan implementation information from multiple initiative teams to develop reports, forecasts, models, and recommendations; assess progress, dependencies, risks, funding assumptions, organizational impacts, and emerging issues.

• Analyzes and interprets strategic plan implementation information to identify trends, gaps, interdependencies, sequencing considerations, resource implications, and emerging risks, and develops insights that support planning, prioritization, and decision-making.

• Maintains budget planning inputs, coordinating information from initiative teams, tracking funding assumptions, supporting high-level costing and funding estimates for proposed strategic initiatives, and supporting alignment between implementation plans, project/operational initiative planning, and budget submissions to support Strategic Plan budget planning and funding analysis.

• Advances strategic plan planning and reporting cycles by continuously improving related tools and products and synthesizing implementation information into governance materials and inputs for Senior Leadership Team and Council-level reporting.

• Supports Strategic Plan planning cycles by maintaining and continuously improving planning tools, templates, schedules, budget planning materials, and reporting products that enable consistent monitoring and follow-up across initiatives.

• Assesses organizational readiness, adoption considerations, and change impacts across strategic plan initiatives, identifying risks, gaps, dependencies, and mitigation considerations that may affect successful implementation and strategic plan outcomes.


III. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Education and Experience

• Completion of an undergraduate degree in business management, public policy administration or other relevant areas.

• Relevant professional experience supporting program, project, portfolio, business planning, or strategic initiative implementation, including monitoring, reporting, and risk or dependency tracking.


Organizational Competencies
Consistently demonstrate CNO’s Organizational Competencies:

• Innovation – Curiously cultivate new ideas with a desire to learn and a collective focus on the best outcome.

• Integrity – Conduct every interaction with fairness, honesty, and mutual respect.

• Collaboration – Work with the right people at the right time to make the best-informed decision.

• Well-being – Care for the physical, mental, spiritual, and emotional needs of ourselves and others.


Job Competencies, Knowledge, Skills

• Analytical and Critical Thinking – uses the ability to synthesize complex information into meaningful reports and insights; analyzes and interprets information to identify themes, readiness considerations, organizational impacts, potential barriers and areas that may require attention or mitigation.

• Communication – uses effective communication skills to convey complex information in a clear and concise manner when creating reports for Council, Senior Leadership Team or Chief Officers that support organizational planning and decision-making; adjusts communication delivery and approach when difficulties with understanding arise; adapts messaging for different audiences; considers perspectives of others when expressing ideas.

• Problem Solving – identifies patterns and trends related to a problem; evaluates impacts, risks, obstacles and benefits before recommending a solution; recommendations relate to implementation planning such as reassessment of sequencing, additional coordination occur between affected teams.

• Relationship Management – builds and establishes collaborative working relationships with system partners when supporting Strategic Planning cycles or budget planning; provides coordination of information from the imperative lead, program manager, project teams and other business areas to get input and support on strategic imperatives, considers future objectives and needs.

title: Coordinator, Health, Safety, & Environmental
description:
Job Type:

Regular

Plains is an industry-leading transportation and midstream provider specializing in transportation, storage, processing and marketing solutions for crude oil. We own an extensive network of pipeline transportation, terminalling, storage and gathering assets in key oil producing basins and transportation corridors and at major market hubs in the United States and Canada. The company is headquartered in Houston, Texas.

We’re on the lookout for passionate self‑starters who thrive in fast‑moving, collaborative, and innovative environments.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities


Incident Investigations and Event Management

  • Lead, facilitate, and support investigations.
  • Determine the appropriate level and scope of investigation based on the nature, severity, and potential significance of an event.
  • Conduct preliminary information-gathering activities to determine whether a formal investigation is necessary.
  • Support events that may require information gathering, documentation preservation, or legal hold activities even when a formal investigation report or Lessons Learned Bulletin (LLB) is not required.
  • Coordinate with HSE, Operations, Legal, and other stakeholders, as appropriate, throughout the investigation process.
  • Ensure investigation records, findings, and associated action items are accurately documented and maintained.
  • Monitor the timely completion and quality of incident investigations and associated corrective actions.
  • Coordinate with third-party investigator on investigations, when necessary.

High Risk Potential Program (HRPP)

  • Lead and coordinate the High Risk Potential Process (HRPP) to promote consistent identification, evaluation, review, and organizational learning from events with high-risk potential.
  • Facilitate monthly HRPP meetings with HSE and Operations to review applicable events, discuss findings, identify trends, and determine opportunities for improvement.
  • Facilitate quarterly HRPP meetings with Leadership to communicate significant events, key findings, recurring themes, and organizational learning opportunities.
  • Develop and coordinate quarterly HRPP Lessons Learned Bulletins (LLBs) to communicate significant findings and lessons across the organization.
  • Develop and maintain the HRPP Annual Book, consolidating significant events, lessons learned, trends, corrective actions, and other relevant information from the program.
  • Partner with the Training organization to develop HRPP-related training sessions and supporting materials.

Maximo Incident Management

  • Provide functional support and subject matter expertise for HSE incident management processes within Maximo.
  • Conduct field visits and Microsoft Teams training sessions related to incident management.
  • Provide ongoing assurance, coaching, and training to field personnel regarding the documentation of HIDs, Near Misses, and Incidents in Maximo.
  • Perform daily reviews of incident management entries to evaluate data quality, completeness, timeliness, and adherence to established requirements.

Release Reviews

  • Participate in release-review meetings and support the evaluation of applicable release events.
  • Review event information and ask appropriate questions to ensure events are accurately understood, documented, and classified.
  • Update Maximo records as necessary to accurately reflect event details and investigation outcomes.
  • Ensure applicable 7000.1 and 7000.2 documentation is aligned with information recorded in Maximo.
  • Evaluate events to determine whether an investigation by the HSE investigation team is warranted.
  • Work with Operations and HSE stakeholders to resolve discrepancies in event information or documentation.

Regulatory and Organizational Reporting

  • Support U.S. RIMS reporting and associated incident-management requirements.
  • Maintain accurate and complete incident information necessary to support internal and external reporting requirements.
  • Collaborate with appropriate stakeholders to validate incident information prior to reporting.
  • Support audits, assurance activities, and management reviews related to incident management and investigation processes.

Lessons Learned and HSE Communications

  • Develop clear, concise, and actionable communications based on investigations, significant events, emerging trends, and organizational learning.
  • Develop and distribute:
    • Lessons Learned Bulletins (LLBs).
    • HSE Bulletins.
    • HSE Alerts.
  • Work with subject matter experts and stakeholders to validate technical content prior to publication.
  • Translate complex investigation findings into practical learning that employees and leaders can apply in the workplace.
  • Maintain consistency and quality across incident-related HSE communications.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, Engineering, Industrial Technology, or a related discipline preferred.
  • Equivalent combinations of education, professional certifications, and relevant HSE experience may be considered.

Experience

  • Experience in Health, Safety, and Environmental programs, with emphasis on incident management, investigations, or operational safety.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting or facilitating incident investigations and root cause analyses.
  • Experience working with incident-management systems or enterprise asset-management systems such as Maximo preferred.
  • Experience analyzing HSE performance metrics, incident trends, and corrective-action data.
  • Experience developing and delivering HSE training to field and leadership audiences.
  • Experience working collaboratively with Operations, HSE, Training, and other cross-functional stakeholders.

Knowledge, Skills, and Competencies


The successful candidate should demonstrate:

  • Strong incident investigation and root cause analysis capabilities.
  • Ability to evaluate complex events objectively and ask effective investigative questions.
  • Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills.
  • Ability to recognize systemic and organizational contributors to incidents.
  • Knowledge of incident classification, risk ranking, corrective-action management, and organizational learning principles.
  • Strong data-quality and records-management discipline.
  • Ability to analyze HSE metrics and identify meaningful trends.
  • Strong written communication skills, including the ability to develop professional investigation reports, Lessons Learned Bulletins, HSE Bulletins, and HSE Alerts.
  • Strong presentation, facilitation, and training skills.
  • Ability to interact effectively with field employees, Operations leaders, HSE professionals, and senior leadership.
  • Ability to manage multiple investigations, projects, and recurring program responsibilities simultaneously.
  • Strong attention to detail and follow-through.
  • Ability to handle sensitive, confidential, and legally significant information appropriately.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and applicable incident-management systems.
  • Working knowledge of Maximo and CauseLink preferred.
  • Successful HSE representation in Incident Management Convergence and Mobility initiatives.
  • Cleared criminal history (background) and satisfactory reference checks
  • Compliance with the Company’s drug and alcohol policy including pre-employment D&A testing.
  • This position is not eligible for employment-based visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. for the duration of their employment

The selected candidate will be eligible for company benefits including Medical, Dental, Vision, Paid Time Off (PTO), and Free Parking.

title: Payment Anomaly Detection Business Analyst - Officer
description:
Who we are looking for:

We are looking for a detail-oriented payments analyst to support implementation and subsequent BAU operations of the payment anomaly detection capability. The role will perform hands-on business analysis, rule validation, test execution, process documentation and operational readiness, then transition after go-live into day-to-day operations ,rule performance, exception and control support.


Why this role is important to us?

Anomaly detection must identify unusual payments without introducing unnecessary processing delays or additional approval, audit, or client-communication activities. This role provides the detailed analysis and validation required to make the capability accurate, usable and operationally sustainable.

Join us if contributing to our Payments Business Risk and Resiliency Programs is a challenge you are up for.


What you will be responsible for

  • Document business requirements, user stories, process maps, decision tables and acceptance criteria under the direction of the workstream lead.
  • Develop and maintain detailed rule definitions, thresholds, tolerances, reason codes, expected outcomes and test cases.
  • Analyse sample and historical payment data to validate rule logic, identify data-quality issues and assess expected alert volumes and false-positive patterns.
  • Execute functional, integration, regression and user acceptance tests across screening, decisioning, case management, UI, reporting and audit functions.
  • Capture defects with reproducible evidence, support prioritisation and retest corrected functionality.
  • Validate queue prioritisation, time-to-cut-off logic, risk tiers, alert grouping, case statuses, client-contact information, templated communications and implementing Agentic AI.
  • Prepare standard operating procedures, quick-reference guides, training materials and operational playbooks for go-live.
  • Support production-readiness activities, access testing, maker-checker controls, audit evidence and cutover planning.
  • After go-live, monitor alerts, rule outcomes, false positives, exceptions, service levels and data issues; prepare analysis for tuning and governance.
  • Align anomaly detection and cyber-response processes so suspicious or incorrect payment activity is triaged effectively during resilience events.
  • Support high-volume events and post-event reviews, ensuring decisions, approvals and evidence are captured.

What we value:

These skills will help you succeed in this role:

  • Payments operations or payments-control experience with strong analytical and documentation skills.
  • Ability to interpret payment data, process flows, business rules and test results.
  • Awareness of SWIFT or ISO 20022 messages, payment rails, cut-offs, screening or fraud controls is beneficial.
  • Disciplined approach to testing, evidence capture, issue management and operational procedures.
  • Strong communication, teamwork and attention to detail.

Education & Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in business, finance, data, technology or a related field.
  • 5+ years of relevant financial services experience.
  • Experience in business analysis, testing, payments operations, fraud or screening is preferred.

title: Psychiatric Technician- Psychiatric Emergency Empath Unit
description:
Location: Generose 2W (GE2W), Psychiatric Emergency Empath Unit

Join our dedicated team in the Emergency Psychiatric Empath Unit, where we provide compassionate, immediate care for individuals experiencing acute mental health crises. Our multidisciplinary team focuses on empathetic support, assessment, and stabilization in a safe, non-judgmental environment. We prioritize patient-centered approaches, integrating evidence-based practices to promote recovery and resilience. Located in the Generose building. The adult treatment area will have 16 chairs and the child adolescent area will have 6 chairs.

The Psychiatric Technician is an integral member of the psychiatric residential, hospital-based psych emergency services team and participates in both direct and indirect patient care for adults and children. At the direction of a registered nurse the Psychiatric Technician promotes involvement in the treatment program. Psychiatric Technicians assist residents in various social, clinical, nutritional, and observational activities to ensure optimal patient outcomes and a safe patient milieu. The Psychiatric Technician role plays a crucial role in ongoing safety observation, assessment of the milieu and identification of escalation of concerning behaviors. The Psychiatric Technician plays a key role in leading social activities, games and crafts that promote patients to engage in milieu and practice therapy concepts they are learning within individualized care plans.

High school graduate or equivalent. At least 21 years of age.

Additional Qualifications:

  • Experience in a psychiatric hospital setting as a mental health or behavioral assistant working with adults and or children -OR- completion of 12 college credits preferred.

  • Basic computer and keyboarding competence with the ability to use Microsoft office suite and or competency with electronic clinic documentation.
  • Demonstrates ability to multi-task under stressful situations.
  • Demonstrates ability to communicate, collaborate and manage relationships with interdisciplinary members while maintaining patient/family centeredness and safety in a timely, efficient, and equitable manner.
  • Basic skills in cleaning, cooking, and meal preparation.

Other required training (first aid, food safe, comorbid disorders, trauma informed care) is offered after hire and must be completed within first 90 days of employment.

Valid driver’s license, and acceptable driving record as defined by policy.

description:

From core custody, accounting, fund administration and shareholder recordkeeping to complete operations solutions and servicing for alternative assets like OTC derivatives, private equity and real estate, SSGD’s tools help our clients make better investment choices and act on growth opportunities.

· Coordinate and manage reporting deliverables, timelines, and stakeholder expectations to ensure accurate, timely, and high-quality completion of client reporting obligations.

  • Serve as a subject matter expert for financial reporting systems and processes by maintaining data integrity, resolving process queries, and providing guidance, support, and coaching to team members.

· Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders across global locations to facilitate issue resolution, obtain required information, and support successful delivery of reporting requirements.

  • Review and enhance reporting processes, documentation, SOPs, process flows, and control frameworks to improve efficiency, consistency, quality, and operational effectiveness.

Effective collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships with internal teams, clients, auditors, and global stakeholders.

A proactive ownership mindset, with a commitment to continuous improvement, knowledge sharing, and delivering high-quality outcomes in a controlled environment.

Education & Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or above in Accounting, Finance, or related discipline.

  • Strong analytical mindset and attention to detail, with proven ability to identify issues, develop solutions, and support informed decision-making.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, with advanced Excel skills including complex formulas, data validation, pivot tables, and financial reporting tools.
  • Strong English written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proven ability to effectively manage multiple priorities, perform under pressure, meet tight deadlines, and consistently deliver high-quality results.

Additional requirements:

  • Overtime may be required during peak reporting periods.
  • Ability to work across time zones when required to support global stakeholders and reporting deadlines.

Job Summary

Naropa University’s Master of Arts in Clinical Mental Health Counseling program seeks an experienced curriculum/content developer to design a 1-Credit hybrid (asynchronous/synchronous) version of the three-credit course CNSG 771E - California Law & Professional Ethics for LPCC Practice during the Spring 2027 course development cycle. This position is for developing the online content only, though there may be the opportunity for applicants to teach the course in a future semester.

CNSG 771E - California Law & Professional Ethics for LPCC Practice

12 Contact Hours

Course Description

This intensive California-specific course prepares out-of-state counseling graduates for registration as an Associate Professional Clinical Counselor (APCC) by covering California statutes, regulations, ethical standards, licensing law, and professional practice requirements established by the California Board of Behavioral Sciences. The course emphasizes practical application of legal and ethical standards through case analysis and clinical decision making.

This structure aligns closely with the statutory topics listed in California law and with common BBS-approved providers.

Job Duties & Responsibilities

· Create an eight-module, hybrid (asynchronous/synchronous) online course in the timeframe of January – May 2027
· Generate (in conjunction with the Office of Educational Technologies) online content, including recorded lectures, practice sessions, and experiential learning activities; textual material; assignments; and assessment rubrics; and

title: Helpdesk Support Specialist
description:
Who We Are

The SecurityMetrics IT Department is a tight-knit team passionate about learning, collaborating, and supporting one another as we solve complex technical challenges. We believe mentorship is a core value, and this role is specifically designed for a technically-minded individual looking to break into the IT field, gain hands-on troubleshooting experience, and open doors for pursuing a career in IT.

The Role: Your Impact

As a Helpdesk Support Specialist, you will be the face of IT support for our team. You’ll provide vital on-site support to employees, build strong interpersonal rapport across departments, and ensure technical issues are addressed promptly and effectively. This is an ideal launching pad for someone with limited IT experience who has a strong drive to learn, manage assets and applications, and develop key technical skills.

Your Mission & Responsibilities

  • Workstation & User Support: Perform employee workstation troubleshooting across a largely Mac-based customer base, with a handful of Linux and Windows systems.
  • Network & Application Management: Diagnose network issues (making minor physical and logical changes) and provide management/support for applications, including user access provisioning.
  • Onboarding & Offboarding: Perform lifecycle tasks for employees, ensuring access is enabled for new hires and revoked for departing employees.
  • Access Control & Facilities: Manage building access controls, including working with other business units to grant correct access.
  • Asset Tracking: Manage company assets to ensure equipment is tracked, maintained, and ready to be deployed.
  • Process Improvement & Engineering Support: Discover, develop, and execute projects to improve IT processes and systems while assisting the IT Engineering team with project work.

Tools You Will Work With

(Prior experience is a plus, but willingness and speed to learn are key!)

  • Operating Systems: macOS, Linux, Windows
  • Applications & Software: Google Workspace, Google Chrome, Zoom, BambooHR, JumpCloud, and others
  • Infrastructure & Hardware: Local networks, access control systems, asset tracking management

What We’re Looking For

Problem-Solving & Communication

  • An interest in computers and how they work.
  • A logical, methodical approach to problem solving.
  • Clear communication with both technical and non-technical individuals.
  • An ability to listen to and be understanding of customer concerns and complaints.

Personality & Work Ethic

  • A desire to learn and succeed in a technical field.
  • A friendly, customer service-oriented personality.
  • A feeling of ownership and responsibility over work performed.
  • Punctuality and promptness during core business hours.
  • And a healthy dash of nerdiness to fit the IT stereotype!

What’s in it for You?

  • Direct Mentorship: Learn directly from senior IT engineers and find mentorship to help grow into more technical IT roles.
  • Hands-on Experience: Gain practical experience troubleshooting workstation and network issues, managing assets, and administering cloud applications.
  • Career Path: Develop key skills in the IT field to prepare for long-term career growth.

• endless career development opportunities including apprenticeships
• friendly, supportive team and the knowledge that you make a huge difference to your community
• access to Stream - a money management app that gives you access to a percentage of your pay as you earn it

A place you’ll belong

We're building diverse and inclusive teams that reflect the communities we serve. We welcome applications from everyone and are committed to creating a workplace where colleagues can feel like they belong, supported by our inclusive policies and the ways we work.

At WGU, data plays a critical role in advancing student success and driving informed decision-making across the university. This role is ideal for an experienced analytics professional who enjoys solving business problems, building scalable reporting solutions, and helping stakeholders make confident, data-driven decisions.

What You'll Do

  • Partner with business leaders, faculty, and cross-functional teams to understand business needs, translate user stories into technical requirements, and deliver analytics solutions that drive action.

title: Business Analyst – Sr (SCCL Governance Framework)
description:
Description

Business Analyst – Sr (SCCL Governance Framework)

Summary:

A business analyst for the Single Counterparty Credit Limits (SCCL) regulation will play a vital role in establishing governance framework, operating procedures and regulatory compliance. The role will act as a key liaison across P2PM, Commercial, Consumer and Capital Markets groups to establish sustainable processes, control routines, data validation standards, and business-as-usual monitoring. The business analyst will partner with IT and Data teams to assist in data validation and testing. The business analyst will help ensure SCCL processes are well governed, auditable, and aligned with internal policies, regulatory expectations, and enterprise risk management practices.

Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Governance Framework: Support the development and maintenance of the SCCL governance framework, including requirements and controls related to credit risk mitigants, funds, economic interdependence, control relationships, and counterparty aggregation.
  • Process Documentation: Draft, maintain, and periodically refresh standard operating procedures, process manuals, operating instructions, desktop procedures, and run-books governing SCCL processes and control activities.
  • Controls and Accountability: Define ownership, RACI matrices, approval workflows, escalation paths, evidence standards, and audit trails to support transparent execution and regulatory defensibility.
  • Process Improvement: Identify and drive process improvement opportunities to reduce operational risk, manual touchpoints, control gaps, data quality issues, and process breaks.
  • Stakeholder Partnership: Coordinate recurring working sessions and governance forums with P2PM, Commercial, Consumer, Capital Markets, Internal Audit, Legal, Compliance, and Reporting teams to maintain alignment on SCCL execution.
  • Training: Create training modules and documentation and facilitate training sessions and process walkthroughs.
  • Stakeholder Requests: Triage, document, and resolve ad-hoc inquiries from regulatory reporting, data, front office partners, and control stakeholders.
  • Testing and Data Validation: Perform business validation and user acceptance testing to confirm accuracy, completeness, consistency and reliability, and fit for regulatory monitoring and reporting.
  • · Data Analysis: Analyze exposure, mitigant and counterparty data from source systems, applications, and downstream reporting environments using Excel, SQL, and other analytical tools.
  • Miscellaneous: Performs other duties assigned.

Following SCCL implementation, the following responsibilities will become part of business-as-usual:

  • Compliance Monitoring: Ensure the daily monitoring is consistently executed and in compliance with approved procedures, internal controls, escalation standards, and regulatory requirements.
  • Key Controls and Metrics: Establish, track, and report key control indicators, data quality metrics, open issues, remediation progress.
  • Business-as-Usual Support: Maintain working knowledge of exposure products, credit risk mitigants, and organizational initiatives that may affect SCCL monitoring or reporting.
  • Change Management: Monitor new products, systems, data feeds, and business initiatives that may affect SCCL processes; assess impacts and coordinate updates to requirements, controls, and documentation.
  • Documentation Maintenance: Update procedures, governance framework, process flows and other documentation based on working sessions and stakeholder feedback.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, project management, finance, computer science or a related field.
  • At least 2+ years of experience in business analysis, process management or a related role.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Governance and Documentation: Experience drafting, maintaining, and enhancing procedures, process maps, control narratives, process manuals, governance documentation, and stakeholder-facing materials.
  • Stakeholder Management: Demonstrated ability to build partnerships, facilitate working sessions, document decisions, and communicate effectively with partners.
  • SQL: Experience with data analysis tools such as MS Excel, SQL etc.
  • Best Practices: Knowledge of process management, procedure governance, control design, audit readiness, issue management, and operational risk reduction practices.
  • Problem-Solving: Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to identify governance gaps, assess operating effectiveness, support audit readiness activities, and evaluate compliance impacts.
  • Exposures and Mitigants: Knowledge or experience of exposure and mitigant products used across the banking industry.
  • Data: Experience in banking or financial services industry working with data for consumer, commercial and investments segments.
  • Project Management: Knowledge or experience in project management methodologies such as waterfall and agile.

title: Animal Control Officer
description:
Come work at a place where we strive to promote and create a safe community. We take pride in living and working in Central Texas and are looking for exceptional talent to join our team.

Job Description:

Duties and responsibilities:

The functions listed below are those that represent the majority of the time spent working in this position. Management may assign additional functions related to the type of work of the position as necessary.

  • Provides daily care for all animals housed at the county shelter, including feeding, watering, cleaning, and monitoring health and behavior.
  • Maintains sanitary and humane conditions within the shelter in accordance with applicable laws, standards, and best practices.
  • Assists with the intake and processing of animals, including documentation, identification, photographing, and microchip scanning.
  • Coordinates or administers basic medical care as needed and facilitates veterinary treatment when required.
  • Manages animal placement efforts, including reuniting animals with owners, facilitating adoptions, and coordinating transfers or rescues.
  • Performs or assists with humane euthanasia in accordance with policy, training, and certification requirements.
  • Maintains accurate shelter records, including intake logs, medical records, disposition reports, and daily statistics.
  • Operates and maintains shelter equipment, kennels, and facilities in a safe and functional condition.
  • Investigates animal bites, ensures proper quarantine procedures, and completes all required reporting.
  • Interviews complainants and animal owners to determine compliance with laws and ordinances.
  • Prepares reports, citations, and case files; may testify in court as required.
  • Guides the public on responsible pet ownership, animal care, and applicable laws.
  • Assists citizens reclaiming animals or navigating adoption processes.
  • Promotes animal welfare and compliance through education and outreach.

Equipment & Safety

  • Operates equipment, including animal control vehicles, radios, capture tools, traps, computers, microchip scanners, and related tools.
  • May use defensive tools, including pepper spray or firearms, when necessary to protect self or others.
  • Assists law enforcement personnel when requested in matters involving animal-related public safety concerns.

Minimum Education and Experience Requirements:

  • High school diploma or GED equivalent.
  • Preferred: Minimum of six (6) months of experience in animal control, animal shelter operations, law enforcement, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.

Physical Demands:

  • Work involves frequent standing, walking, bending, lifting, and handling animals.

  • Regularly requires exertion of 20–50 pounds of force.
  • Requires manual dexterity and coordination in handling equipment and animals safely.
  • Ability to work weekends, holidays, and after-hours as needed.

Unavoidable Hazards (Work Environment):

  • Animals (including aggressive or diseased animals)
  • Extreme temperatures and weather conditions
  • Noise, odors, and cleaning chemicals
  • Zoonotic diseases and biohazards
  • Hazardous or unpredictable situations involving animals or the public

Special Certifications and Licenses:

  • Must possess and maintain a valid state driver’s license with an acceptable driving history.
  • Must be able to read, write, and speak the English language.
  • Required (or ability to obtain within six months):
    • Animal Control Officer Certification
    • Euthanasia Certification
    • Bite Stick and/or Pepper Spray Certification

title: Data Architect / Engineer - Assistant Vice President
description:
Who we are looking for

We are looking for an experienced Data Architect / Data Engineer, Assistant Vice President to provide technical and architectural leadership for enterprise cybersecurity data, analytics, and AI capabilities.

This role will define and deliver scalable data architectures, Lakehouse platforms, data models, integration frameworks, and AI-ready data foundations. The individual will partner with cybersecurity, engineering, architecture, governance, risk, and product teams to transform complex security data into scalable, governed, and actionable solutions.

What you will be responsible for

As a Data Architect / Engineer, you will:

· Architect and deliver scalable Lakehouse and enterprise data platforms, pipelines, data models, and reusable data products.

· Define target-state data architecture, reference architectures, integration patterns, standards, and technical roadmaps.

· Design solutions for large-scale structured, semi-structured, time-series, graph, and unstructured cybersecurity data.

· Establish reusable frameworks for ETL/ELT, ingestion, orchestration, data quality, metadata, lineage, observability, and reconciliation.

· Establish architecture standards for scalability, resiliency, performance, security, privacy, governance, and auditability.

· Design AI-ready data architectures supporting LLMs, RAG, embeddings, vector/semantic search, NLP, knowledge graphs, and intelligent workflows.

· Integrate data across cloud platforms, enterprise systems, cybersecurity platforms, and SIEM/SOAR ecosystems.

· Provide technical leadership through architecture reviews, engineering standards, technology evaluation, and solution governance.

· Partner with stakeholders to translate cybersecurity and business requirements into scalable data and AI solutions.

· Mentor engineering teams and drive reusable architecture patterns, automation, and engineering best practices.

What we value

These skills will help you succeed in this role:

· Strong expertise in Data Architecture, Data Engineering, Cloud Data Platforms, and AI/GenAI.

· Deep understanding of Lakehouse architecture, distributed processing, ETL/ELT, data modeling, integration, data quality, metadata, lineage, and governance.

· Strong hands-on skills in Python, SQL, PySpark, Databricks, Delta Lake, and cloud technologies.

· Experience designing enterprise-scale, secure, resilient, and governed data platforms.

· Practical knowledge of LLMs, RAG, embeddings, vector/semantic search, NLP, knowledge graphs, and responsible AI architecture.

· Understanding of cybersecurity telemetry, SIEM/SOAR, vulnerability management, identity risk, threat intelligence, and incident data.

· Ability to influence architecture decisions and engage effectively with technical teams, architects, product leaders, and senior stakeholders

Education & Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

· 15+ years of experience across Data Architecture, Data Engineering, enterprise data platforms, cloud, analytics, AI, or related technology disciplines.

· Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.

· Proven experience architecting and delivering enterprise-scale data platforms and Lakehouse solutions.

· Strong experience with Python, SQL, PySpark, Databricks, ETL/ELT, distributed processing, data modeling, and AWS or comparable cloud platforms.

· Experience with CI/CD, automated testing, monitoring, data governance, and engineering best practices.

· Experience in cybersecurity, financial services, regulated industries, or large enterprise environments is highly desirable

· Strong written, verbal, analytical, and stakeholder communication skills.

Technical Skills

Skill Area

Expected Capabilities

Data Architecture

Lakehouse, enterprise data modeling, data domains, data products, data contracts, integration patterns, reference architecture, metadata and governance

Data Engineering

Python, SQL, PySpark, Databricks, Delta Lake, ETL/ELT, orchestration, data quality, lineage and observability.

AI & Gen AI

LLMs, RAG, embeddings, vector/semantic search, NLP, knowledge graphs, responsible AI and AI-enabled workflows.

Cloud & DevOps

AWS, CI/CD, Git, automated testing and scalable cloud data processing

Cybersecurity Data

SIEM/SOAR, security telemetry, vulnerability, identity, incident and threat intelligence data.

Visualization & BI

Power BI, semantic models, operational metrics and executive reporting.

Additional Requirements

· This is an individual contributor role with strong cross-functional collaboration expectations.

· The role will require sound judgment when working with sensitive cybersecurity, risk, operational, and regulated data.

· The candidate should be comfortable balancing exploratory data science, production-minded analytical delivery, and stakeholder communication.

Why this role is important to us

Cybersecurity increasingly depends on the ability to engineer, integrate, analyze, and intelligently interpret large volumes of complex security data. This role will bridge Data Engineering, Data Science, Cybersecurity, and AI, building trusted data foundations and intelligent solutions that improve threat detection, risk prioritization, security operations, and enterprise decision-making.

About State Street

State Street is one of the world's leading providers of financial services to institutional investors, including investment servicing, investment management, investment research, and trading. Technology and cybersecurity are critical enablers of our ability to safeguard information, support clients, and operate at enterprise scale.

We value collaboration, innovation, inclusion, and responsible technology. We are looking for technical talent who can solve meaningful problems, communicate clearly, and help build secure, scalable, data-driven capabilities for the future.

State Street is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer.


About State Street


Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.


We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.

title: Healthcare Project Manager
description:
PROCEDEO is seeking an experienced Healthcare Project Manager to lead healthcare construction projects in the Dallas-Fort Worth area. This position is responsible for the successful planning, coordination, execution, and closeout of healthcare construction projects, including work within occupied and operational healthcare environments.

The Healthcare Project Manager has primary responsibility for the financial, technical, operational, and client-service success of assigned projects. This individual will lead project teams and trade partners while coordinating closely with healthcare owners, facility leadership, Infection Prevention, Facilities/Engineering, clinical stakeholders, design professionals, and other project partners.

The successful candidate will bring strong commercial construction project management experience combined with demonstrated knowledge of the unique requirements associated with healthcare construction, including infection-control practices, occupied-facility construction, critical system shutdowns, life-safety requirements, phased construction, and maintaining continuity of patient care and healthcare operations.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Maintain ultimate responsibility for the financial and technical success of assigned projects.
  • Review plans, specifications, and contract documents for accuracy, constructability, scope coordination, sequencing, and potential risk.
  • Establish and maintain baseline and detailed project schedules, including subcontractor activities, owner milestones, inspections, shutdowns, equipment installations, commissioning, and turnover.
  • Track project costs and forecasts and manage change orders, RFIs, owner pay applications, subcontractor pay applications, and other financial controls.
  • Oversee document control, shop drawings, submittals, procurement logs, closeout documentation, and other required project records.
  • Write, negotiate, and administer subcontracts and purchase orders.
  • Manage subcontractor performance and relationships and conduct regular project and jobsite coordination meetings.
  • Lead construction planning and coordination within occupied and operational healthcare environments, including hospitals, medical centers, outpatient facilities, clinics, laboratories, surgical facilities, and other clinical settings.
  • Understand and support implementation of Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) requirements, including barriers, containment, negative air, HEPA filtration, dust control, pressure relationships, temporary partitions, protected pathways, and construction access controls.
  • Coordinate construction activities with healthcare Infection Prevention, Facilities/Engineering, clinical leadership, Security, Risk Management, owners, and other facility stakeholders.
  • Plan and coordinate construction phasing around active patient-care areas while minimizing disruption to patients, visitors, healthcare personnel, and ongoing facility operations.
  • Coordinate critical shutdowns, utility interruptions, tie-ins, demolition, above-ceiling work, temporary conditions, emergency egress, and fire/life-safety requirements.
  • Ensure project planning accounts for sensitive clinical environments such as operating rooms, emergency departments, ICUs, imaging areas, laboratories, pharmacies, and procedural spaces when applicable.
  • Coordinate required shutdown plans, Safe Work Plans, ICRA documentation, interim life-safety measures, and other healthcare-specific construction documentation with the project team.
  • Proactively identify construction activities that could affect patient care, infection prevention, critical systems, emergency operations, or healthcare facility continuity and develop appropriate mitigation plans before work begins.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for healthcare clients and maintain proactive, consistent communication throughout the project.
  • Build credibility and trusted relationships with healthcare owners, facility leadership, Infection Prevention teams, design professionals, consultants, trade partners, and other project stakeholders.
  • Lead project meetings and communicate project status, schedule, financial performance, risks, changes, and upcoming critical activities.
  • Anticipate client needs and proactively resolve issues that could affect project delivery or healthcare operations.
  • Promote collaboration between project management, field operations, safety, quality, preconstruction, and trade partners.

CANDIDATE QUALIFICATIONS

  • Minimum of 5 years of commercial construction project management experience, with significant experience managing healthcare construction projects.
  • Demonstrated experience managing construction within occupied and operational healthcare facilities strongly preferred.
  • Experience with hospital renovations, additions, expansions, new healthcare facilities, outpatient facilities, medical office buildings, clinics, laboratories, or similar healthcare environments.
  • Working knowledge of healthcare construction requirements, including ICRA, infection-control practices, life-safety requirements, construction phasing, shutdowns, utility interruptions, and work adjacent to active patient-care areas.
  • Detailed understanding of construction project sequencing, scheduling, budgeting, cost control, procurement, and change management.
  • Advanced understanding of construction drawings, specifications, constructability, and coordination between architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and specialty healthcare systems.
  • Ability to negotiate, write, execute, and administer subcontract agreements and purchase orders.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage complex projects involving multiple stakeholders and competing operational priorities.
  • Strong leadership, problem-solving, organizational, written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Ability to build effective relationships with healthcare owners, design teams, facility personnel, clinical stakeholders, subcontractors, and internal project teams.
  • Must work effectively in a team environment and demonstrate a strong commitment to client service.
  • Experience with CMAR and/or Design-Build delivery methods preferred.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Microsoft Project, Bluebeam, and Procore.
  • Valid Driver's License.
  • Travel and/or relocation may be required based on project assignments.

EDUCATION

  • Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, Construction Technology, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.
  • Equivalent education and substantial directly applicable healthcare construction experience may be considered.

PREFERRED HEALTHCARE EXPERIENCE & CREDENTIALS

  • Formal ICRA healthcare construction training or certification.
  • Experience coordinating with healthcare Infection Prevention and Facilities/Engineering departments.
  • Knowledge of applicable NFPA and healthcare fire/life-safety requirements.
  • Familiarity with The Joint Commission, DNV, CMS, and other healthcare regulatory or accreditation requirements as they relate to construction activities.
  • Experience managing construction in highly sensitive clinical environments.
  • OSHA 30-Hour Construction certification preferred.

Employment Benefits:

Employee Benefits include a negotiable salary, 401K (with company match), full medical/dental/vision insurance, paid time off, life and disability insurance, paid maternity and paternity leave, tuition reimbursement, HSA and FSA medical plans as available to fulltime company employees.


About the PROCEDEO Group:

PROCEDEO is a national leader in alternative project delivery methods for architecture and construction, as well as cutting-edge construction technology within the education and municipal sectors. We oversee full portfolios of capital projects for K-12 districts, municipalities and universities from conception through all phases of procurement to completion. Our team prides itself on providing exceptional service while remaining attentive to client needs. We specialize in delivering projects efficiently and effectively, maintaining a client-focused approach. PROCEDEO is an equal employment opportunity company. title: Cost Capture Analyst
description:
Who are we?

Here within the @one Alliance we are a totally collaborative organisation made up of our eight partner companies (Anglian Water, Balfour Beatty, Barhale, Binnies, MMB, MWH Treatment, Skanska and SWECO) and our extended supply chain, delivering over half of Anglian Water’s capital investment programme.


Now in our most exciting and challenging Asset Management Period yet, known as AMP 8, this will see us deliver a programme of work larger than we’ve ever delivered before. We are driving change, empowering us to set global benchmarks and build a better environment, with the opportunity to offer enhanced growth and development to our workforce. We’re looking to build on our existing teams with an environment for career progression.


With a variety of challenging and complex projects, it is essential we implement the most innovative and pro-active commercial practices possible, providing an industry-leading end-to-end Commercial facility across the @one alliance. We are looking for an Analyst to join our Cost Capture Team.

What will you be doing as our new Cost Capture Analyst?

We’re looking for someone to support both our infrastructure and non-infrastructure business streams.

As an experienced Cost Capture Analyst, you’ll be largely self-governing and self-motivating to provide for all Cost Capture deliverables at Delivery Milestone. You’ll have awareness of commercial, programme and costing processes as well as suggesting change to systems. As a key member of all the delivery teams, you’ll regularly communicate with those teams and the Anglian Water’s Cost Intelligence team.

You’ll understand the importance of the cost capture function, which involves the determination of all assets installed on a project and assessing the cost of those assets. It is not only a requirement of OFWAT (governing body of the water industry), but also provides the business with historic data from which future commercial assessments can be made.

If you’re new to the discipline, then we’ll provide a structured training programme which will support your development as a Cost Capture Analyst.

Key responsibilities:

  • Understand the project deliverables by interrogating the BIM model, drawings, and supplier quotations by liaising with the relevant project team.
  • List all assets installed, take off quantities and enter the data into the Asset+ database under the appropriate WBS (plant group) code.
  • Using the quotations, procurement information, standard product prices and historic data, assess asset costs and enter results in Asset+.
  • Use Commercial reports, SAP downloads and estimate data to assess Prelim and Overhead costs.
  • Ensure that proper records are kept and maintained so financial information for audits and cost assurance is readily available.
  • Liaise with Project Coordinators to prioritise the work schedule.
  • Using historic data provide feedback, when necessary, to assist in future project costing.

A little bit about your skills, experience and behaviours….

If you’re looking to launch a successful career in Cost Capture, it would be fantastic if you hold an Engineering or QS degree or have previous relevant experience. However, more important than your educational and experience background, is your enthusiasm to learn and add value to our operations.

You should be numerate with good analytical skills and be comfortable working in Microsoft Office (especially Excel). You should enjoy working in a Team environment and you’ll be open to and able to communicate with a wide range of audiences. You should be comfortable working to deadlines and have good organisational skills.


If the opportunity to join one of Anglian Waters key frameworks appeals to your aspirations, please apply today!


Our Approach to Diversity & Inclusion

At the Anglian Water’s @one Alliance, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where every individual feels valued, respected, and empowered to contribute their unique perspectives and talents. We believe that diversity enriches our team, fuels innovation, and drives success. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, and actively encourage individuals from underrepresented groups to apply. We are dedicated to creating an environment free from discrimination and bias, where everyone has equal opportunities for growth and advancement. Join us in creating a culture where diversity is celebrated, and inclusion is the norm.


Alongside this we want to ensure that all candidates have an equal opportunity to showcase their abilities during the interview process. If you require any specific accommodations or adjustments due to a disability or any other individual circumstances, please do not hesitate to let us know.


Our vision

A collaborative alliance, driving change. Empowering us to set global benchmarks and building a better environment for our customers. We strive to:

Empower our people; Delight our Customers; Embrace digital transformation; Deliver brilliance.


Our Values

To bring environmental and social prosperity to the region we serve through our commitment to Love Every Drop we:

Build trust; Do the right thing; Are always exploring

title: Motor Claims Handler
description:
As a Motor Claims Handler, you will own the final stage of the credit hire claim process. Once the hire period has ended, you will investigate the claim, challenge what is being charged, and negotiate a fair settlement that minimises the financial impact for our customers.

Who We Are

Revantage, a Blackstone Real Estate portfolio company, is a global provider of corporate services. With a corporate purpose of ‘In Pursuit of Better, Revantage delivers value-added services and world-class talent for Blackstone Real Estate portfolio companies, spanning diverse asset classes, including residential, logistics, office, hospitality and retail sectors. Headquartered in Chicago, the company’s footprint extends across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific.


Rooted in a commitment to collaboration and inclusivity, Revantage goes beyond traditional corporate services and acts as a trusted partner. Across offerings that include finance, technology, human resources and operations, Revantage proactively anticipates stakeholder needs, recruits exceptional talent and enables its business partners to thrive.


What We Value: Our Culture


Creating a culture that inspires change and momentum requires the right team. We know what it takes to lead an industry, and are looking for leaders who seek constant growth, want to excel, and continuously improve themselves and the industry. The culture at Revantage is built on our shared core values and commitment to be:


· Achievers – We hold ourselves to high standards to enable our team’s success


· Enthusiasts – We face challenges with optimism and believe anything is possible


· Leaders – We commit to continuously improve our performance


· Learners – We learn from others and our challenges and successes


· Partners – We deliver value and positive impact to our partners

Why This Role Is Valuable

The Sustainability Data Senior Analyst - Intelligence Senior Analyst is vital in advancing our sustainability initiatives by transforming complex data into clear, actionable insights and supporting our data management programs. This role enhances decision-making by engaging stakeholders and providing visual representations of sustainability metrics, enabling stakeholders to track progress, improve data quality, identify trends, and make informed choices.


This position is based out of Revantage’s Bangaluru, India office.

How You Add Value

Data Collection


  • Own the initial collection and review of sustainability data in partnership with the Revantage Sustainability team, ensuring submissions meet completeness and preliminary quality standards.
  • Coordinate across a broad stakeholder network to drive complete and timely data submissions ahead of comprehensive review and quality assurance by Revantage Sustainability.
  • Contribute to the design and enhancement of Excel- and platform-based data collection and reporting templates, incorporating conditional formatting, data validation, and completeness checks to improve accuracy and efficiency.

Data analysis and interpretation


  • Take ownership of analyzing and interpreting large sustainability datasets, including energy consumption, renewable energy, water consumption, green building certifications, and greenhouse gas emissions.
  • Transform and enrich datasets to identify gaps, inconsistencies, outliers, and errors, ensuring data integrity.
  • Utilize data processing tools such as MS Excel and Alteryx to meet analysis requirements efficiently.

Data Quality Assurance


  • Drive initial data quality reviews by proactively identifying gaps, inconsistencies, outliers, and errors that could affect data integrity.
  • Engage directly with data-submission stakeholders to investigate variances and obtain clear explanations when established thresholds are triggered.
  • Own data cleaning and validation activities, helping ensure datasets are accurate, complete, and ready for analysis and reporting.

Data visualization

  • Partner with project managers to maintain and enhance interactive dashboards and reports, ensuring they continue to meet evolving stakeholder needs.
  • Enable effective self-service analytics by keeping dashboards accurate, current, intuitive, and easy to navigate.

Effective communication & collaboration


  • Build strong working relationships across cross-functional teams, including data analysts, developers, and project managers, to advance shared project objectives.
  • Engage with stakeholders to understand business requirements, address uncertainties, and gather feedback, ensuring outputs align with user expectations.
  • Serve as a key point of coordination for data submitters across Blackstone portfolio companies and joint venture partners, maintaining clear and consistent communication throughout the submission and review process.
  • Apply agile practices to facilitate iterative development, allowing for quick adaptation to changing requirements.

Sustainability Team Support


  • Create high-quality team presentations (PowerPoint) and deliver responsive analysis for ad hoc information requests.
  • Coordinate key administrative activities and team priorities as needed to support effective execution.
  • Conduct targeted research on sustainability-related topics, synthesizing findings into relevant and actionable information for the team.

What You Bring To The Role

Required:

title: Order Checker
description:
At Lineage, helping to feed the world is more than a job – it’s a purpose we live every day. Lineage is the world’s largest and most innovative provider of temperature-controlled logistics solutions.

To support increasing customer demand, we are currently seeking an Order Checker to ensure our products entering, and leaving our warehouse are correct so that we can prepare for these items to be distributed to our customers.

This will be working within the Coldstore at our Hams Hall depot.

Available shifts: 3 on 3 off nights, 18:00-06:00

Rate of pay: £12.94 per hour


Shift allowance: £55 per week

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Review load/batches delivered to verify quantity and type of material.
  • Create and apply labels showing quantity and type of material/product.
  • Report amount of materials and items transported, received, and distributed.
  • Weigh or count items for distribution within the warehouse to determine and ensure we meet company standards and customer expectations.
  • Report damages and claims to management completing inventory control.
  • Process inbound/outbound orders safely and accurately.
  • Loading and unloading vehicles using power pallet trucks.
  • You will do this in a cold environment – approximately minus 25 Celsius – just like working in the freezer; but we provide full PPE.
  • Use MHE to run pallets around the warehouse.

Who we're looking for:

  • Accuracy is important so someone who likes to get things right first time.
  • Things are heavy so you will need to lift up to 18kg (that’s about 10 bags of sugar).
  • You to be able to communicate clearly with other team members in English.
  • Having some experience loading and unloading vehicles within a warehouse environment is advantageous but not essential as full training will be given.

Why Lineage?

We are a global company with more than 22,000 employees spanning 20 countries and more than 400 locations across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and South America.

At Lineage Logistics, we have a shared purpose; we are transforming the food supply chain to eliminate waste and help feed the world. This means working at Lineage is not just a job – it’s an opportunity to innovate and put your mark on how food moves from the farm to dinner tables around the world. As a member of our team, you will be a critical link in the food supply chain.

Our shared purpose drives everything we do in all parts of our organisation, from the warehouse floor to the office. Our team members are passionate about the impact they make every single day.

We are an equal opportunities employer and positively encourage applications from persons regardless of sex, race, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender reassignment, religion or belief, marital status, or pregnancy and maternity. At Lineage we also recognise that Ex-Military, veterans, and military families have great experience with transferable skills and core values that can add significant value to our organisation.

Benefits

As a Lineage team member, we aim to provide everything you and your family need to thrive. That’s why we offer competitive rates of pay, paid time off, skills training, and development opportunities to grow a long and fulfilling career with us. This is enhanced by recognition schemes (so that your hard work won’t go unnoticed), plus the chance to make your salary go even further with our cycle-to-work scheme and preferential rates for loans and savings courtesy of a leading credit union.

Your everyday wellbeing is also important to us, so we will provide you with all the protective equipment you need to be safe and comfortable at work, and you will have access to a free 24/7 employee assistance phone line, which offers confidential counselling and advice. With all of this offered against the backdrop of a fun and social environment in which you will be supported by a team who enjoy helping each other in achieving their goals, we are confident you will excel with us.

title: Physical Security Specialist
description:
Job Title: Physical Security Specialist

Location: Tempe, AZ

Division: Operations

Department: Director of Infrastructure Security & Compliance


About Us:

Quantum Computing Inc. (QCi) (Nasdaq: QUBT) is an innovative, integrated photonics company that provides accessible and affordable quantum machines to the world today. QCi products are designed to operate at room temperature and low power at an affordable cost. The Company’s portfolio of core technology and products offer unique capabilities in the areas of high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, cyber security as well as remote sensing applications.


Scope of the Job:

QCi is seeking a Physical Security Specialist to help protect its facilities, personnel, and classified and proprietary information. This hands-on role will manage day-to-day physical security operations, including access control, video surveillance, alarm systems, and visitor management, while supporting the company’s Facility Clearance (FCL) and compliance with the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM) and Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) requirements. The ideal candidate combines practical security-systems experience with a strong understanding of industrial security regulations and works effectively with employees, visitors, vendors, and government representatives.


Duties / Responsibilities:

  • Security Systems Management: Standardize, manage, and monitor security systems, including video surveillance, electronic badge systems, alarms, and related maintenance or upgrades.
  • Physical Access Control: Administer physical-access controls, including employee and visitor badges, access permissions, restricted areas, key control, and periodic access reviews.
  • Inspections and Risk Assessments: Conduct physical-security inspections, annual self-inspections, risk assessments, and corrective-action tracking to address identified deficiencies.
  • Incident Investigation and Reporting: Investigate and document security incidents, access violations, suspicious activity, and system alerts, escalating reportable matters to the Security Director and appropriate authorities.
  • Facility Clearance and Regulatory Compliance: Support the company’s Facility Clearance (FCL) and compliance with the NISPOM, DCSA requirements, and applicable government security regulations.
  • Personnel Security: Assist with personnel security activities, including clearance processing, briefings, debriefings, visit requests, and maintaining records in DISS and NISS.
  • Visitor Control: Coordinate visitor-control procedures, including identity verification, access authorization, escort requirements, and retention of visitor records.
  • Security Procedures and Documentation: Help develop and maintain standard operating procedures, site security plans, and related records, keeping them current with regulatory and operational changes.
  • Security Education and Awareness: Support security awareness training, insider-threat program activities, and required initial and annual refresher briefings.
  • Vendor and Audit Coordination: Coordinate with security vendors, contractors, and facilities personnel on installations and service, and help prepare for DCSA security reviews and internal audits.


Required Skills & Experience:

  • 3–5 years of industrial or physical security experience, preferably with a cleared defense contractor
  • Working knowledge of the NISPOM (32 CFR Part 117), DCSA requirements, and applicable government security regulations
  • Hands-on experience administering access-control, video surveillance, and intrusion alarm systems
  • Familiarity with personnel security processes, including clearance processing and the DISS and NISS systems
  • Strong investigative, documentation, and record-keeping skills with close attention to detail
  • Ability to handle sensitive and classified information with discretion and sound judgment
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and proficiency with Microsoft Office
  • U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance

Additional Preferred Skills:

  • Active DoD Secret clearance or higher
  • Bachelor’s degree in criminal justice, security management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Hands-on experience processing clearances and maintaining records in DISS and NISS
  • CDSE or industry certifications such as the Security Fundamentals Professional Certification (SFPC), Industrial Security Oversight Certification (ISOC), or ASIS Physical Security Professional (PSP)
  • Experience preparing for and supporting DCSA security reviews
  • Experience with enterprise access-control and video management platforms
  • Familiarity with ITAR/EAR export controls and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) handling requirements
  • Experience in a manufacturing, semiconductor, or research and development environment

Quantum Computing Inc. (QCi) is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Incumbent(s) in this position may be required to perform other duties and special assignments not specifically stated above. Statements outlined in this section are designated as essential job functions in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990.

title: RF Product Manager
description:
About GF:

GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, power-efficient and high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. With global manufacturing operations across the U.S., Europe and Asia, GF is a trusted and holistic technology partner for customers around the world. GF’s talented, global team remains focused every day on security, longevity, and sustainability. For more information, visit .


Summary of Role:

The RF Product Manager is responsible for the profitability and growth of GlobalFoundries’ RF technology portfolio, including RF SOI, SiGe BiCMOS, RF GaN, and related wireless connectivity solutions. This role drives the business strategy, commercial success, and customer adoption of the portfolio and serves as a key interface between customers, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Operations, Finance, and executive leadership.

The RF Product Manager develops and executes product and market strategies, evaluates customer requirements, analyzes competitive positioning, drives design-win activities, and manages product lifecycle execution from concept through high-volume manufacturing. This position requires a strong combination of semiconductor technical knowledge, business acumen, financial analysis, strategic thinking, and customer engagement skills.


Essential Responsibilities:

  • Own the profitability and growth of the RF GaN business line and support the broader RF technology portfolio.
  • Define and execute product-line strategies to achieve revenue, profitability, market-share, and customer-adoption objectives.
  • Develop and implement programs and strategies that support business and financial objectives.
  • Develop and maintain technology and product roadmaps aligned with customer requirements, market trends, and business objectives.
  • Identify target customers and build and strengthen strategic customer and external partner relationships.
  • Identify, prioritize, and drive strategic customer engagements, design wins, and business growth opportunities across target RF markets.
  • Lead business-case development, including TAM/SAM analysis, revenue forecasting, ROI assessment, and investment prioritization.
  • Partner across Product Development, Technology Development, Manufacturing, Marketing, Sales, and Finance to support successful product execution and commercialization.
  • Establish product positioning, value propositions, pricing strategies, and go-to-market plans.
  • Analyze competitive offerings, technology trends, and market dynamics to identify opportunities for differentiation and growth.
  • Support customer meetings, executive reviews, roadmap discussions, technical workshops, and business negotiations.
  • Monitor product financial performance, including bookings, revenue, gross margin, wafer demand, pricing, and capacity requirements.
  • Drive product lifecycle management, including product introduction, qualification, customer ramp, and end-of-life planning.
  • Provide business updates, forecasts, and strategic recommendations to executive leadership.
  • Collaborate with ecosystem partners, EDA vendors, IP providers, and other external organizations to strengthen the RF technology portfolio.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable internal policies and legal requirements across areas of responsibility.

Other Responsibilities:

  • Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs.

Required Qualifications:

  • Master of Science degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Materials Science, Semiconductor Engineering, Business, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 8 years of experience in semiconductor product management, marketing, business development, product engineering, technology development, or related technical leadership roles.
  • Demonstrated understanding of RF semiconductor technologies, including RF SOI, SiGe BiCMOS, RF GaN, CMOS, or related wireless technologies.
  • Experience developing business cases, financial models, market forecasts, and long-range strategic plans.
  • Strong customer-facing experience with the ability to communicate effectively with both technical and executive audiences.
  • Experience working across cross-functional organizations in a global environment.
  • Ability to travel up to 25% domestically and internationally.
  • Strong analytical, presentation, communication, and project management skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering with an emphasis in RF devices, circuits, or systems; MBA is a plus.
  • Experience in wireless connectivity, cellular infrastructure, SATCOM, aerospace and defense, Wi-Fi, mobile RF front-end, optical communications, or high-speed communications markets.
  • Experience designing and characterizing RF devices and circuits.
  • Experience with foundry business models and semiconductor manufacturing operations.
  • Knowledge of semiconductor cost modeling, pricing strategy, and product portfolio management.
  • Experience supporting executive business reviews and strategic planning activities.
  • Familiarity with RF system concepts, device technologies, and market analysis tools.

  • Experience using business intelligence and analytics tools.
