title: Senior Enterprise Architect
description:
We are seeking a visionary, hands-on Senior Enterprise Architect to join our enterprise architecture team and help shape the future of our software platforms. This role will provide technical leadership across software architecture, enterprise modernization, scalability, cloud adoption, and the strategic integration of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

The ideal candidate is an accomplished software engineer and architect with a deep understanding of designing, building, and evolving complex enterprise software systems. This individual will work across architecture, engineering, product, data, security, and business teams to establish technical direction, define architectural standards, and translate complex business challenges into practical, scalable, and secure software solutions.


This is not a data science or AI model-development role. However, we are looking for a software architect who understands how to apply and integrate AI capabilities into real-world enterprise software. Candidates may come from a strong software engineering, architecture, platform engineering, or AI engineering background; deep expertise in statistics, model training, or academic machine learning is not required.


The Principal Software Architect will remain hands-on while operating at an enterprise level—developing prototypes, reference implementations, frameworks, scaffolding, and complex technical solutions that help engineering teams adopt architectural patterns and deliver high-quality software. The role will also serve as a technical thought leader and mentor, helping establish a culture of engineering excellence, innovation, and continuous modernization.

Experience in the insurance industry is a strong plus.


Key Responsibilities

  • Architectural Leadership: Design and collaborate with engineering teams to build resilient, highly scalable, secure, maintainable, and observable distributed software systems as part of a collaborative enterprise architecture team.
  • Hands-On Architecture & Development: Develop architectural prototypes, reference implementations, scaffolding, frameworks, algorithms, and other technical solutions that demonstrate architectural patterns and accelerate engineering adoption and delivery.
  • Enterprise Modernization: Lead architectural direction for software modernization initiatives, including legacy application transformation, application decomposition, cloud adoption, platform evolution, API strategies, integration, and modernization of critical enterprise systems.
  • AI & Generative AI Architecture: Define and lead the technical strategy for incorporating AI and GenAI capabilities into enterprise applications and platforms. Evaluate and integrate LLMs, third-party AI services, AI agents, and other emerging AI technologies where they provide meaningful business or engineering value.
  • AI-Enabled SDLC: Identify opportunities to leverage AI to improve developer productivity, software development, testing, code quality, documentation, application modernization, and other areas of the SDLC. Establish reusable patterns, standards, and guardrails that enable engineering teams to adopt AI safely and effectively.
  • Technical Roadmap & Governance: Establish architecture patterns, reference architectures, frameworks, engineering standards, and technical roadmaps across software development and AI adoption, ensuring alignment with enterprise strategy, business objectives, security requirements, and industry best practices.
  • Cloud & Distributed Systems: Provide architectural leadership for cloud-native applications and distributed systems, with an emphasis on scalability, resilience, availability, performance, observability, and operational excellence.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with product management, engineering, data, security, infrastructure, and business leadership to translate complex business problems into practical, elegant, and scalable technical solutions.
  • Technical Influence & Mentorship: Serve as a technical mentor and thought leader for architects and engineering teams. Promote strong software engineering practices, rigorous code quality, design excellence, performance optimization, and continuous improvement.
  • Technology Evaluation: Evaluate emerging technologies, software frameworks, cloud-native services, AI capabilities, and architectural approaches to continuously evolve the organization's technology landscape.
  • Leadership: The ideal candidate is able to see the big picture, understand the details, and help teams turn architectural vision into working software.

Required Qualifications

  • 12+ years of professional experience in software engineering, software architecture, or a related technical discipline.
  • 4+ years operating at a Principal Engineer, Principal Architect, Enterprise Architect, Lead Architect, or similar senior technical leadership level within a complex enterprise environment.
  • Deep, hands-on experience designing and building enterprise-scale software applications and distributed systems.
  • Strong software development background with significant experience in one or more modern programming languages such as Java, Python, .NET/C#, or similar.
  • Demonstrated expertise with modern architectural patterns, including microservices, event-driven architecture, API-driven systems, distributed systems, cloud-native architecture, and domain-driven design.
  • Experience architecting and delivering systems that require high availability, scalability, resiliency, security, performance, and operational excellence.
  • Experience with cloud platforms and cloud-native services, preferably Microsoft Azure.
  • Demonstrated ability to move between high-level architecture and hands-on technical implementation, including developing prototypes, reference architectures, frameworks, or production-quality code.
  • Strong understanding of software development lifecycle practices, DevOps, CI/CD, automated testing, observability, and modern engineering practices.
  • Practical experience with AI and/or generative AI in software applications or engineering environments.
  • Ability to evaluate AI technologies and determine how they can be effectively integrated into enterprise software and existing technology ecosystems.
  • Exceptional communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence engineers, architects, product leaders, business stakeholders, and executive leadership.
  • Demonstrated ability to establish technical direction, build consensus, and make sound architectural decisions in a complex enterprise environment.
  • The successful candidate will be an architect and technical leader who can operate comfortably at multiple levels—from discussing enterprise technology strategy with executives to reviewing architecture and code with engineers.

title: Student Conduct Advisor
description:
We are here to launch, advance, and evolve careers — join us and make an impact.

Job Description


About Bow Valley College

For 60 years, Calgary’s college has grown to prepare 14,000 students annually for meaningful careers in health care, social services, business, technology, and creative industries. Every program has a Work Integrated Learning requirement, ensuring students contribute to the workplace before they graduate. With a strong focus on advanced simulation training and Alberta’s evolving needs, Bow Valley College’s new Health Care Centre of Excellence is working to expand space and programs, aimed at graduating four-times as many health professionals annually by 2036.


Proudly recognized as one of Canada’s Top 50 Research Colleges, we combine innovative learning with hands-on experience. Home to Alberta’s only major e-sports arena and a state-of-the-art digital production hub. Learn more about the opportunities Bow Valley College creates for students, Calgary, and Alberta at .

Position Summary

Bow Valley College is seeking a skilled and compassionate Student Conduct Advisor to join the Student Services team. Reporting to the Manager, Accessibility and Conduct, this role plays a critical part in supporting student well-being, promoting accountability, and maintaining a safe and inclusive learning environment.


As the Student Conduct Advisor, you will lead the administration of student conduct and sexual violence processes, provide conflict resolution support, conduct investigations, and develop educational programming that promotes awareness of student rights and responsibilities. This role requires sound judgment, strong case management skills, and the ability to navigate complex and sensitive situations with professionalism, fairness, and care.


Working closely with students, faculty, staff, and external partners, you will help ensure that concerns related to non-academic misconduct, sexual violence, and student conflict are addressed in a manner that is fair, trauma-informed, and aligned with institutional policies and legal requirements.



What You'll Be Doing:


Lead Student Conduct Investigations and Case Management: Manage reports of non-academic misconduct and alleged contraventions of the College's Sexual Violence Policy, serving as the primary investigator for complex and sensitive cases. Receive and assess reports, determine appropriate policy responses, conduct interviews with complainants, respondents, and witnesses, review evidence, consult with relevant stakeholders, and prepare investigation findings and outcome documentation.


Apply principles of procedural fairness throughout the conduct process while exercising sound professional judgment and independent decision-making. Conduct ongoing assessments of student well-being, including mental health, suicide risk, and threat assessments when required, to support student and campus safety. Attend Student Appeal Committee hearings and remain current on emerging legal issues, case precedents, accommodation requirements, and best practices in student conduct administration.


Provide Conflict Resolution Support and Student Guidance: Serve as a primary resource for students, faculty, and staff seeking support in navigating conflict and behavioural concerns. Provide conflict coaching, guidance on available resolution options, and support for informal resolution processes in accordance with college policies and procedures.


Facilitate restorative and alternative dispute resolution approaches when appropriate and assist employees in responding to concerns through informal interventions. Connect students with appropriate on-campus and community resources to support their academic success, personal well-being, and safety, ensuring a coordinated and student-centered approach to case management.


Develop Educational Programming and Prevention Initiatives: Design, deliver, and evaluate educational programs that increase awareness of student conduct expectations, sexual violence prevention, conflict resolution, restorative practices, and available supports. Collaborate with departments across the College to provide training and presentations for students, faculty, and staff on relevant policies, procedures, and responsibilities.


Develop educational materials and outreach resources in both print and digital formats to promote understanding of student conduct processes and available services. Support policy awareness initiatives and assist with communicating policy updates and procedural changes to the College community.


Manage Conduct Data, Reporting, and Compliance: Maintain accurate and confidential case records in accordance with college policies, professional standards, the Protection of Privacy Act (POPA), the Access to Information Act (ATIA), and records retention requirements. Manage incoming reports and related documentation, ensuring information is appropriately tracked, documented, and maintained within relevant databases and student information systems.


Support the collection, analysis, and reporting of student conduct and sexual violence data to identify trends, evaluate services, and inform continuous improvement initiatives. Contribute to the development of assessment and reporting processes that support effective decision-making and compliance with legislative and institutional requirements.


Contribute to Campus Safety and Student Success: Work collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders to support a safe, respectful, and inclusive learning environment. Provide expertise and consultation on student conduct matters, contribute to institutional initiatives related to student well-being and safety, and support the broader goals of Student Services through participation in projects and initiatives as assigned.



What Sets You Apart

You are a thoughtful and highly skilled student affairs professional who is committed to balancing student support, accountability, and community safety. You excel at navigating complex situations, conducting fair and thorough investigations, and supporting individuals through challenging circumstances with empathy, professionalism, and respect.


You possess strong interpersonal and communication skills and are comfortable working with diverse populations and perspectives. Your ability to assess risk, manage sensitive information, facilitate conflict resolution, and apply policy with consistency and fairness allows you to build trust and credibility with students, employees, and stakeholders across the College.



Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field, plus 2-5 years of related work experience.
  • Experience in a related setting where skills and expertise required have been demonstrated.
  • Directly related professional student affairs experience, including knowledge of development theory and conduct processes is preferred.
  • Experience related to case management, including investigations.
  • Skilled in risk assessment and intervention.
  • Understanding of restorative justice.
  • Understanding of procedural fairness and knowledge of how to implement.
  • An equivalent combination of directly related education and experience may be considered.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A high degree of unique problem-solving and independent judgment.
  • A thorough understanding of the legal precedents and federal mandates pertaining to student conduct administration is critical.
  • Advanced training and experience in resolving disputes.
  • The ability to exercise considerable discretion and judgment in sometimes highly volatile situations is essential.
  • Ability to manage and complete tasks in a timely manner and maintain accurate records and files as demonstrated by past accomplishments or experiences.
  • Excellent written communication, interpersonal, and public speaking skills, and the ability to work effectively with diverse populations.

Closing Date: Until Filled


This opening is a temporary (AUPE) position with an expected end date of Aug 3, 2027. Please note all successful candidates will be required to provide copies of government issued identification and proof of educational qualifications upon hire and may be required to provide an enhanced police information check. If your education was received internationally, we will require you to provide an international education assessment through IQAS, WES, or one of the other nationally designated organizations upon hire.

Union :

AUPE

Diversity and Inclusion Commitment
Bow Valley College is strongly committed to fostering diversity and inclusion within our community. We welcome applications from qualified candidates who would contribute to the further diversification of our employees including, but not limited to, visible minorities, Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities and persons of any sexual orientation or gender identity.

title: Associate Director, Client Relationship - USA
description:
JOB SUMMARY / INTRODUCTION

To develop and maintain relationships with an assigned portfolio of technology clients, with a particular focus on digital infrastructure, data centers and semiconductors. The role requires a strong understanding of sector business models, capital expenditure requirements and financing structures, including data center development, construction and operating financings. Working closely with Product Teams, Group Credit, Treasury and Global Markets, the role holder will originate and deliver suitable financing and advisory solutions, provide high-quality client service and support sustainable revenue growth.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Client and Market Analysis
  • Participate in the financial analysis conducted on clients and their respective industries/ markets to identify potential opportunities and risks.
Client Relationship Management
  • Visit and provide continuous support to clients in order to satisfy their daily transactional requirements, enquiries, and documentation needs.
  • Follow-up with other sub-departments/ departments on credit/ facility requests to ensure clients’ requests are met on-time.
  • Assist the coverage banker / team in making some basic calls to clients and following up with them on the services provided by FAB and any other requirements as directed by the Head of CMB or Executive Directors / Directors, in order to build capability of the CB sub-department.
  • Review facility documents and follow-up with clients to ensure that they submit renewed or missing documents on-time.
  • Convey potential client acquisitions to Head of CMB or Executive Directors / Directors while providing them with clients’ needs and the conducted due-diligence in order to conduct credit assessments/ appraisals and pass them for approval.
  • Works closely with the Client Service team to guarantee the highest quality of service to the clients in the portfolio.
  • Achieve individual and team financial performance targets.
  • Identify & develop cross selling opportunities and increase the cross-sell ratio with key clients.
  • Ensure Account Plans are prepared and maintained for all key clients.
  • Ensure all clients’ files /documents are maintained.
  • Ensure all credit reviews are submitted on time and agreed conditions are met.
  • Adhere to process KPI’s and, ORM, BCP & Internal Audit requirements.
Day-to-Day Activities
  • Assist the Head of CMB or Executive Directors / Directors in the day-to-day administrative and transactional activities such as client calls, documentation follow up, updating pipeline, and any other activities in the unit/team to ensure continuity of work and the delivery of effective and high quality outputs.
  • Manage and follow up on KYC and compliance requirements in order to ensure consistency with the Bank’s KYC and AML policies and regulatory requirements.
Credit Approval
  • Collects credit request and documents from the clients in the portfolio and conduct initial analysis to check plausibility against preliminary rejection criteria and submit necessary documents to Group Credit in order to facilitate the credit analysis and approval process.
  • Assists Group Credit in development of the CAs through provision of relevant client documents and inputs, and reviews it in the end, in order to ensure quality and completeness of all CAs before approval.
  • Ensures the quality of the credit portfolio is maintained by assisting in reviewing proposals and identifying and assessing all risks inherent in credit exposures.
Internal Collaboration
  • Develops a close working relationship with all departments including Product partners (Debt Markets, Global Transaction Services, Islamic Banking, Corporate Finance, and Treasury & Global Markets Group) in order to contribute to cross selling opportunities.
Policies, Systems, Processes, and Procedures
  • Follow all relevant sub-departmental policies, processes, standard operating procedures, and instructions so that work is carried out in a controlled and consistent manner.
MIS and Reports
  • Assist in the preparation of timely and accurate statements and reports to meet the unit’s requirements, policies, and standards.
Specific Accountability
  • Develop and manage relationships across the digital infrastructure ecosystem, including data center developers and operators, hyperscalers, cloud and connectivity providers, semiconductor companies, equipment manufacturers and financial sponsors.
  • Originate, structure and execute financing solutions for data center development, construction, expansion and operation, including corporate, acquisition and project-related facilities.
  • Assess sector-specific credit considerations, including contracted revenues, customer concentration, power availability, construction and ramp-up risk, technology cycles, supply-chain exposure and capital intensity.
  • Maintain current market intelligence on data center capacity, power and land constraints, cloud and AI-driven demand, semiconductor investment cycles and relevant financing activity.
  • Coordinate with product, credit and risk partners to deliver lending, capital markets, treasury, transaction banking and advisory solutions tailored to technology clients.
Frameworks, Boundaries, & Decision Making Authority
  • Functions within the framework and boundaries of Group policies as well as overall organisational and governance frameworks.

REQUIREMENTS / QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Qualification
  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance or related discipline.
Minimum Experience
  • Minimum 5 years of relevant corporate or investment banking experience, with demonstrated coverage or transaction experience in technology and digital infrastructure.
  • Direct experience in data center financing is required; meaningful exposure to the semiconductor sector is strongly preferred.
  • Track record of supporting the origination, credit assessment, structuring and execution of complex financing transactions.

Preferred / Beneficial

  • Master’s degree in Business Administration is preferred.
  • Meaningful exposure to the semiconductor sector is strongly preferred.

title: Program Director
description:
Program Director

Location: Harpeth Primary Assessment Center
Job Type: Full-Time
Pay: $90,000
Schedule: Full-time; includes administrator-on-duty responsibilities and occasional extended, evening, or weekend hours.


About Youth Opportunity & Harpeth Primary Assessment Center

Youth Opportunity is a nationally recognized leader in residential and behavioral health services for youth. We help young people build foundations for success and independence through physical and emotional well-being, positive social and family relationships, and education. We invest in our employees through teamwork, professional development, and opportunities for growth.

At Harpeth Primary Assessment Center, our team provides assessment services and structured, trauma-responsive programming to support youth safety, stabilization, and individualized care. Clinical, medical, educational, case management, and direct care teams work together to assess each youth’s needs and coordinate appropriate next steps.


Benefits

  • Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance available after 60 days of employment.
  • 401(k) with a 100% employer match up to 4% of your salary, available after 60 days, with immediate vesting.
  • Paid time off—earn 4 hours each pay period—and 7 paid holidays.
  • Free prescription delivery.
  • Tuition reimbursement and professional development opportunities.
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
  • A supportive, mission-driven work environment.


About the Role

We are seeking a skilled and compassionate Program Director to lead daily operations at Harpeth Primary Assessment Center. Working under the direction of the Executive Director, this position oversees program administration, staffing, service coordination, safety, and compliance.

The Program Director supports timely assessments, quality services, and positive outcomes for youth while promoting staff accountability, effective communication, and a safe, trauma-responsive environment.


Key Responsibilities


Program Operations and Compliance

  • Oversee daily operations across all program departments to ensure safe, efficient, and effective services.
  • Implement program goals, operational priorities, and performance expectations established by the Executive Director.
  • Monitor staffing, schedules, admissions, discharges, and service delivery to ensure timely and appropriate care.
  • Ensure compliance with the Contract Provider Manual, licensing rules, accreditation standards, contractual requirements, and applicable regulations.
  • Serve as the on-site resource for program policies and procedures and ensure consistent implementation.
  • Maintain organized, audit-ready records, reports, schedules, logs, and documentation systems.
  • Develop standard, holiday, and alternative program schedules and monitor staff adherence, including adherence to the school schedule.
  • Facilitate daily Morning Management Meetings, maintain meeting documentation, and participate in afternoon leadership meetings.
  • Establish and communicate the Administrator on Duty schedule and ensure staff know how to access the Clinical on Call schedule.
  • Coordinate major visits, audits, and reviews and communicate operational needs, risks, and recommended solutions to the Executive Director.
  • Manage resources responsibly and maintain budget performance within approved targets.


Staff Leadership and Supervision

  • Provide leadership, supervision, and support to managers, supervisors, teachers, clinicians, direct care staff, case managers, nursing staff, and other assigned employees.
  • Promote professionalism, accountability, ethical conduct, trauma-responsive care, and a positive staff culture.
  • Participate in recruitment, hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, and corrective action in collaboration with Human Resources and the Executive Director.
  • Develop staffing schedules for Executive Director approval, participate in weekly staffing meetings, and ensure required staffing ratios are maintained at all times.
  • Plan effective coverage across operations, medical, clinical, education, and other departments.
  • Monitor attendance, dress code, active supervision, and appropriate staff interactions with youth.
  • Ensure timely completion of on-the-job training plans, coaching sessions, annual performance evaluations, and required staff training.
  • Oversee biweekly Operations Meetings and facilitate monthly All Staff Meetings, including participation in quarterly all-campus meetings.
  • Ensure staff understand and follow documentation, incident reporting, confidentiality, and safety requirements.


Clinical and Medical Service Coordination

  • Ensure clinical and psychological assessments are timely, accurate, and consistent with the program’s service model and required level of care.
  • Coordinate services among clinical, medical, educational, case management, and direct care teams.
  • Monitor admissions, referrals, treatment planning when indicated, crisis response, discharge planning, and continuity of care.
  • Collaborate with clinical leadership to support individualized, evidence-based, trauma-responsive, and strengths-based services.
  • Conduct biweekly coaching sessions with the Clinical Director and Lead Nurse to review service trackers, timeliness, trends, barriers, and needed follow-up.
  • Ensure required medical and dental screenings and visits are completed within Department of Children’s Services guidelines.
  • Review youth alert status, precautionary observation, restraint authorizations, and related documentation for timely completion and appropriate follow-up.
  • Support multidisciplinary participation in treatment team meetings, Child and Family Team Meetings, restraint reviews, and other required meetings.
  • Participate in monthly reviews with each discipline and regional support to address monitoring outcomes, quality improvement goals, and corrective strategies.


Safety and Risk Management

  • Maintain a safe, clean, and appropriate environment for youth, staff, and visitors.
  • Complete daily facility walkthroughs, documented weekly Environmental Safety Inspections, and monthly walkthroughs with the Executive Director and Regional Support Manager.
  • Ensure compliance with emergency response, crisis intervention, infection control, medication safeguards, and environmental safety procedures.
  • Serve as the point of contact for facility incidents and provide real-time reporting to the Executive Director and executive leadership team.
  • Oversee incident response, required notifications, preservation of evidence, and completion of reporting documentation before the end of the shift.
  • Complete camera reviews of critical incidents, restraints, and youth altercations within 24 hours.
  • Review incidents through video footage, interviews, statements, and documentation; coordinate findings and final reports with the Executive Director.
  • Ensure emergency plans remain current and required drills, debriefings, and safety reviews are completed.
  • Strengthen active supervision, identify incident trends, and oversee corrective actions to reduce risk.


Communication, Youth Rights, and Program Improvement

  • Communicate organizational priorities, policy changes, performance expectations, and operational decisions clearly and consistently.
  • Maintain effective relationships with families, legal guardians, referral sources, community partners, and oversight agencies.
  • Escalate significant incidents, staffing concerns, maintenance issues, licensing matters, and other operational risks promptly.
  • Represent the program in meetings, case consultations, audits, and community discussions as assigned.
  • Protect youth rights, dignity, privacy, and confidentiality while promoting respectful and culturally responsive services.
  • Oversee grievances and responses, address initial youth appeals, review complaint trends, and ensure timely resolution.
  • Support family engagement, youth participation in care, access to services, and continuity of care.
  • Recommend improvements to staffing, services, safety practices, and program operations.
  • Support program development, strategic planning, and quality improvement efforts that advance positive youth outcomes.


Other Duties Include

  • Maintain a high standard of role-model behavior for youth.
  • Participate in required training, leadership meetings, committees, and professional development.
  • Report concerns involving inappropriate youth-to-youth or staff-to-youth relationships.
  • Report physical interventions and unusual incidents according to established requirements.
  • Perform other duties as assigned or needed.


Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university.


  • Experience: At least three years of experience working in a residential setting with children who have serious emotional disturbances or substance abuse concerns. Prior supervisory experience in a related setting is preferred.


  • Knowledge: Working knowledge of chemical dependency, substance abuse, and physical, sexual, and emotional abuse, including the ability to assist with youth assessments.


  • Leadership: Ability to supervise staff, coordinate services, manage competing priorities, and maintain a safe, accountable program environment.


  • Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills and the ability to work effectively with coworkers, families, referral sources, agency representatives, and youth.


  • Professionalism: Ability to handle sensitive situations diplomatically and demonstrate respect for professional ethics, cultural differences, gender, and disabilities.


  • Certification: Current First Aid/CPR certification or the ability to obtain it.


Physical Demands

  • Ability to move throughout the property and participate in youth activities.
  • Ability to meet the physical and emotional demands of supervising and supporting youth.
  • Ability to transport youth or staff.
  • Ability to meet applicable state health requirements regarding communicable diseases, consistent with the law.
  • Ability to pass the required physical techniques evaluation and written certification examination.


Other Requirements

  • Must maintain a valid state driver’s license and a safe driving record.
  • Must meet required state and local criminal background check requirements.
  • Must be available to occasionally work extended, evening, or weekend hours.

title: Data Scientist
description:
CURRENT EMPLOYEES - Please apply using "Jobs Hub" in Workday. This career site is for external applicants only.

Job Description

Job Summary


The Data Scientist supports PROPWR’s power generation operations by developing advanced analytics, predictive models, and data‑driven insights that improve asset performance, reliability, and operational efficiency. This role works closely with engineering, operations, and maintenance teams to analyze large datasets from power generation assets, SCADA systems, and condition‑monitoring platforms. The Data Scientist transforms raw operational data into actionable insights that reduce downtime, optimize maintenance, and enhance fleet‑wide decision‑making.


Responsibilities

  • Analyze large datasets from power generation assets, SCADA systems, sensors, and historian platforms.
  • Identify trends, anomalies, and performance deviations impacting asset reliability and availability.
  • Validate and improve data quality across operational systems and data pipelines.
  • Develop predictive models for equipment health, failure probability, and maintenance planning.
  • Build forecasting models for generation output, performance, and reliability.
  • Support reliability engineering by providing data‑driven insights into failure mechanisms and asset risks.
  • Conduct hypothesis testing and statistical analysis to validate assumptions and guide engineering decisions.
  • Build dashboards, KPIs, and performance reporting tools for engineering and operations teams.
  • Translate complex analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for non‑technical stakeholders.
  • Partner with Operations, Maintenance, and Engineering to turn insights into operational improvements.
  • Support root cause analysis (RCA) investigations with data‑driven evidence and modeling.
  • Work with reliability engineers to integrate predictive analytics into maintenance strategies.
  • Document models, assumptions, methodologies, and business impact.
  • Maintain version control, code quality, and reproducibility standards.
  • Support deployment of models into production environments when applicable.
  • Stay current with emerging analytics tools, machine learning techniques, and power‑generation technologies.
  • Maintain compliance with Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) policies by attending all required HSE training sessions, safety meetings, and always utilize proper Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
  • Other duties as assigned

Job Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, or related field.
  • 3–7 years of experience in data science, analytics, or applied machine learning.
  • Strong experience with: Python or R; SQL
  • Statistical modeling and machine learning techniques
  • Time series data analysis
  • Experience working with operational or industrial datasets.
  • Ability to communicate complex analytical concepts clearly and effectively.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in power generation, energy, utilities, or industrial operations.
  • Referenced from uploaded document:
  • “Experience in power generation, energy, utilities, or industrial operations.”
  • Familiarity with SCADA, plant historian data, or condition monitoring systems.
  • Experience with asset performance analytics or maintenance optimization.

  • Experience deploying models into production environments.
  • Exposure to reliability engineering concepts (RCM, FMEA, RCA).

This role requires strong expertise in Oracle Database administration and a willingness to develop skills across PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, and cloud-based database technologies. The engineer will support availability, performance, security, automation, and resiliency initiatives while contributing to continuous service improvement within a highly regulated financial services infrastructure environment.

Your Primary Responsibilities:

This Database Engineer will:

  • Support database lifecycle activities, including upgrades and decommissioning.
  • Provide support for Development, QA, Client Testing, and Production environments through the ServiceNow ticketing system.
  • Participate in root cause analysis (RCA) for database incidents and issues.
  • Support database performance tuning, capacity planning, and proactive health monitoring.
  • Execute database backup, recovery, and disaster recovery validation activities.
  • Participate in automation initiatives using scripting and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) methodologies.
  • Support database security controls, vulnerability remediation, and compliance requirements.
  • Assist with production deployments, release management, and change implementation activities.
  • Monitor database infrastructure using enterprise observability and monitoring platforms.
  • Participate in incident management, problem management, and post-incident reviews.
  • Collaborate with application, infrastructure, cloud, and cybersecurity teams.

Talents Needed for Success:

  • Strong expertise in Oracle databases (19c and 21c), with a solid understanding of database architecture, administration, support, and high-availability environments.

  • Hands-on experience supporting Oracle RAC, ASM, and Oracle Enterprise Manager (OEM) Grid Control/Cloud Control for monitoring and management.

  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to perform root cause analysis and resolve complex issues.
  • Ability to work independently with a high degree of ownership while adhering to established processes and standards.

title: Senior Counsel - Litigation
description:
Description

Summary

Huntington Bank has an exceptional opportunity for a talented litigation attorney to join its dynamic and growing Legal Department. Using thoughtful legal analysis, strategic thinking, and business acumen, you will partner with business leaders, risk partners, and Legal Department colleagues to oversee a diverse portfolio of litigation, threatened litigation, investigations, subpoenas, and other contested matters involving Huntington and its affiliates.

The ideal candidate will have substantial litigation experience, sound business and legal judgment, and the ability to communicate effectively at all levels of the organization. In addition to overseeing individual matters, this attorney will play a key role in managing Huntington's overall litigation portfolio, reporting on trends and litigation exposure, and leading the Legal Department's eDiscovery function.

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Oversee litigation and pre-litigation matters by assessing legal and business risks, selecting and managing outside counsel, developing strategy, directing resolution efforts, and providing guidance in alignment with Huntington's legal, operational, financial, and reputational objectives.
  • Partner with internal stakeholders to investigate claims, develop factual records, identify and prepare witnesses, preserve evidence, coordinate discovery, and support dispute resolution.
  • Lead the Legal Department's eDiscovery function, overseeing preservation and collection efforts, discovery and review processes, eDiscovery vendor relationships and technology, and ongoing enhancement of information governance and litigation support capabilities.
  • Help manage Huntington's broader litigation portfolio by developing and analyzing litigation and legal spend data, monitoring trends and legal risks, and using data-driven insights to manage exposure, improve decision-making, and strengthen litigation prevention efforts.
  • Prepare and deliver matter assessments, exposure analyses, reserve recommendations, and other reports to Legal Department leadership, senior management, risk committees, and other stakeholders.
  • Collaborate across the Legal Department, control functions, and business segments to identify, manage, and mitigate enterprise legal risk, and perform other duties as assigned.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree and Juris Doctor.
  • Eligible to be licensed as corporate counsel or admitted to practice law in the state (Ohio preferred) where job will be located.
  • 5+ years of relevant in-house or law firm experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience handling litigation involving financial institutions.
  • Ability to assess risk, develop litigation and resolution strategies, and provide practical, business-oriented advice with limited supervision.
  • Experience managing legal budgets and controlling spend, using databases and other technology in legal matters, and applying data and analytics to support legal risk management.

title: Director of Finance
description:
Why We're Here

We believe heartfelt, human connections make people's lives better. Especially the people who work here.

Our founder, Bill Kimpton rebelled against impersonal, generic hospitality that makes people feel disconnected. He initiated a new boutique hotel standard and environment where people could connect, from the heart. That was the goal then, and it is still our purpose today.

Your work here has meaning. You're here to improve the lives of coworkers, guests, owners, communities, and together we make that happen. It's what drives all that we do. Every day you can improve lives in your own, unique way and you can expect the same in return. It all starts with you.

How We're Different

Our San Francisco-born entrepreneurial spirit and zest for life kick started this culture in 1981, and it shines through to this day.

It all flows from you. The lively, rebellious, genuine you - with your diverse background, talents, experiences, and plucky personality - is fully welcome, and celebrated here. Because we know that when people can be themselves at work, they shine.

That's what we seek out and celebrate. It's people of all kinds who share a knack for creativity and self-leadership. People who don't need to be told what to do to get things done. People who have an innate passion for making others' lives better.

It adds up to a work environment that's a bit quirky, irreverent, exciting, uncommon, empowering, and downright exceptional. Guests feel it; you'll feel it too.

What You'll Do

As an Area Director of Finance at Kimpton, you're a strategic partner who works with General Managers and Directors of Operations to provide financial expertise and achieve business goals. You direct accounting and control functions at your area properties while ensuring timely reporting of operating results and maintaining the integrity of the management information system.

Some of your responsibilities include:

  • Recruit, train, support and mentor Directors of Finance (DOFs) in your region to be true business partners.
  • Review of financial documents and monthly P&L packages prior to issuance.
  • Complete quarterly balance sheet reviews in Blackline and communicate any outstanding issues and/or liabilities regional leader.
  • Work in conjunction with Ops, Sales, and Revenue teams to complete area scrubs of budgets prior to submission to the regional team.
  • Build and maintain good relationships with all asset managers and attend all owner reviews.
  • Monitor hotel cash flow projections and ensure we are aligned with funding and distribution requirements per the HOA.
  • Ensure Sales and Use Tax laws are being followed and provide leadership for your teams with respect to tax audits.
  • Plan and coordinate all openings and transitions in your area to include the opening checklist, stub budgets, proration schedules, recruiting, hiring and training all finance staff.
  • Actively participate on the area team and collaborate with fellow Area DOFs on projects, policies, and procedures, etc.
  • Provide accounting teams with the resources, training, and empowerment to carry out their responsibilities. Develop each person's talents and skills to their full potential to improve their contribution to the success of the business.
  • Monitor financial performance by ensuring internal controls are in place, monitoring controls to ensure maximum flow and profit, ensuring DOFs are performing, etc.

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's Degree in Accounting or Business Studies is preferred. Master's Degree and/or CPA is a plus.
  • 3 to 4 years of director-level experience in hospitality finance is preferred.
  • Outstanding communication skills and the ability to implement strategic plans.
  • Excellent financial modeling, project management, and critical thinking skills with a strong work ethic.
  • Prior experience with PeopleSoft or similar accounting package, SAP/BPC is preferred.
  • Strong computer skills and proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (with an emphasis on Excel).

title: Senior Geomodeller
description:
Location: Edmonton or Calgary, Alberta

Employment Type: Permanent - Full Time

Salary Range: T4, Level 6, $130,050 - $153,000 per year. The final compensation for this position will be determined based on individual factors, including education, qualifications, experience, and internal equity.


Senior Geomodeller


The Opportunity­­


The Alberta Energy Regulator (AER) is seeking a Senior Geomodeller to join the Alberta Geological Survey (AGS) within our Geoscience Innovation team. In this role, you will apply advanced geomodelling expertise to some of Alberta's most important subsurface challenges, including induced seismicity, basin-scale geological characterization, and strategic geoscience modernization initiatives. This role is a critical piece of AGS’ geospatial intelligence capabilities.

In this role you will will be a major contributor to both strategic and hands-on work across multi-disciplinary projects related to oil and gas, minerals, groundwater and other natural resources. You will work alongside data management experts, data scientists, geologists and geophysicists, remote sensing experts, reservoir engineers, as well as regulatory specialists, business stakeholders, and IT partners to develop geological models and technology architectures that support both regulatory decision making and enhance subsurface characterization and knowledge development.

You will leverage and evolve the Geological Framework of Alberta along side vast archives of industry and AGS data to place Alberta at the forefront of modern, 3D-integrated, geospatially-aware, and AI-enabled subsurface intelligence capabilities. Beyond delivering technical work, you will play a key role in strengthening AGS's internal modelling capability by sharing technical knowledge with staff, advancing modelling standards, and helping shape the future direction of geomodelling within the organization. This role offers a unique opportunity to influence major provincial geoscience initiatives while helping build sustainable technical capacity for the future.


What your day-to-day will look like:

  • Contribute to the development of geological and geomodelling solutions and apply advance geomodelling techniques to subsurface characterization projects associated with disposal, reservoir performance, induced seismicity assessment, and regulatory priorities.
  • Develop and maintain regional and field-scale geological models to support strategic basin management. Contribute structural and stratigraphic modelling expertise to basin analysis activities and broader geological interpretation projects
  • Develop repeatable workflows that can be applied across multiple geological settings.
  • Advance integration between geomodelling, geospatial, and enterprise data initiatives. Collaborate with internal subject matter experts to strengthen connections between geological models, geospatial datasets, and enterprise information systems.
  • Identify opportunities to modernize AGS geomodelling practices. Evaluate current modelling approaches and recommend practical improvements related to workflows, chronostratigraphic and lithostratigraphic frameworks, uncertainty management, reproducibility, and technical assurance.
  • Provide senior technical review and quality assurance. Support model governance, documentation, uncertainty analysis, and consistency across AGS modelling projects.
  • Provide technical coaching and mentorship to AGS staff. Work alongside geologists, geomodellers and reservoir engineers to build modelling competency through project-based learning, technical reviews, and knowledge transfer.

What we’re looking for in you:

  • University degree in Geology, Geological Engineering, Earth Sciences, Geoscience, or a related discipline.
  • Registered, or eligible for registration, as a Professional Geoscientist (P.Geo.) or Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) in Alberta.
  • 7+ years in the energy industry, with progressive related experience in geomodelling or a related field.
  • Extensive experience developing and interpreting geological and geomodelling projects in sedimentary basin settings, at regional- and basin-scale, ideally related to induced seismicity, reservoir characterization, disposal, and subsurface risk assessment.
  • Experience integrating geological, geophysical, engineering, and other spatial datasets into defensible subsurface interpretations. Experience working with stratigraphic frameworks, facies/property modelling, and geostatistics.
  • Strong understanding of uncertainty assessment, model validation, and geological quality assurance practices. Experience establishing modelling standards, technical assurance frameworks, and enterprise modelling practices is considered an asset.
  • Demonstrated expertise with industry-standard geomodelling platforms such as Petrel and related geological modelling software. Experience with Leapfrog is preferred.
  • Proven ability to mentor technical staff and communicate complex geological concepts to multidisciplinary audiences.
  • Strong interpersonal, collaboration, and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Ability to work independently while balancing multiple priorities in a dynamic technical environment.
  • Familiarity with public-sector geoscience organizations and regulatory environments is considered an asset.

Additional Information:

  • All applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada at the time of application.
  • Occasional travel between Edmonton and Calgary may be required.
  • Should an individual with the required qualifications not be available, applicants with closely related qualifications may be considered. As a result, the position may be redesigned and/or reclassified.
  • If you need accommodation during any stage of the recruitment process, please email PeopleServices@aer.ca. Information relating to the need for accommodation and accommodation measures will be addressed confidentially.

What we offer you:

  • The ability to leverage your expertise and critical thinking skills to contribute in wide-ranging, challenging, and complex work.

title: EXECUTIVE, FINANCE
description:

This role requires attention to detail, a strong understanding of financial reporting, and effective coordination with various stakeholders.

  • Timely Financial Reporting – Ensures the accurate and timely preparation of financial reports for the company or business unit.

  • Operational Efficiency – Manages payment processing, petty cash disbursements, and banking operations efficiently.
  • Compliance with Policies – Adheres to internal policies and procedures, including tax compliance.
  • Support in Financial Closing – Assists in preparing closing reports and other month-end activities.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts Handling Account Payables and Receivables

  • Ensure timely processing and update of accounts payable and receivable in line with company policies, tax legislation, and internal procedures.
  • Process unpaid bills, contractor claims, and other transactions related to accounts payable.
  • Review and update journal entries, debit/credit notes, and ensure timely reconciliation of A/R and A/P against the General Ledger (GL).

Banking Updates

  • Review and reconcile collections and related treasury functions to ensure accuracy and timeliness.

  • Summarize monthly financial status by preparing detailed income statements and financial position reports.
  • Assist in the preparation of Cash Flow Reports and Group Reporting (GRP) within the required timeframes.
  • Prepare fixed asset schedules, debtor reports, and creditor reports for monthly account closings.

Prepare Accounts Reconciliation and Journals

  • Prepare and monitor Bank Reconciliation within the agreed timeline after receiving the bank statement.
  • Monitor daily cash flow movements and fund transfers to ensure sufficient funds for operations.
  • Perform creditor and debtor reconciliations on time and ensure all discrepancies are resolved promptly.

Assist in performing journal entries for monthly account closing processes.

  • Administration Related Matters / Ad-hoc Assignments
  • Perform general administrative duties such as managing mail, dispatching documents, and managing office stationery and filing systems.
  • Assist in ad-hoc duties and other tasks assigned by the Head of Department (HOD) or immediate superior.

  • Tax Compliance – Familiarity with tax requirements and internal procedures for compliance.
  • Accounting Systems & Software – Proficiency in accounting systems and spreadsheets for reconciliation and reporting.

  • Microsoft Excel – Strong skills in Excel for data analysis, reporting, and reconciliation.
  • Accounting Software – Familiarity with accounting systems and ERP tools used for financial reporting and reconciliation.
  • Banking and Payment Platforms – Experience with banking platforms for payment processing and monitoring transactions.

Qualifications & Experience

Educational Background

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Finance, Accounting, or related field.

Experience Requirements

  • At least 1-2 years of experience in a similar role within finance or accounting.
  • Familiarity with tax legislation, accounts reconciliation, and financial reporting is preferred.
  • Basic knowledge of cash flow management and banking operations is an advantage.

title: Risk Specialist (ORM) - Contractual
description:
Work for the IMF. Work for the World.

The International Monetary Fund is the apex International Organization at the heart of supporting the stability of the International Monetary and Financial System. The IMF continues to mature its Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework to bring the scope and operations in line with those in other major organizations and international bodies. The scope of the ERM framework covers all key activities of the Fund, including surveillance, lending, and capacity development (CD).

The Office of Risk Management (ORM) is at the center of these efforts and has the lead in developing and supporting implementation of a strengthened ERM framework at the Fund. This includes development of additional methodologies and tools to identify, assess, analyze, and monitor risk, including new risk methodologies and techniques, and their use by Area, Functional, and Support departments; and producing reports on the Fund’s risk profile at regular intervals. ORM is also tasked to highlight areas where additional risk analysis or mitigation efforts are needed and complements risk management policies and practices in operational departments. A key objective is enhanced risk-based decision support across the organization. To enable this, ORM is also responsible for developing Fund training in risk management, strengthening the governance around the risk management function and fostering a culture of risk acknowledgment in the organization. ORM will also provide an independent challenge of enterprise risk information and assessments of Departments.


The successful candidate will use quantitative and qualitative analytical skills, knowledge of risk assessment tools, and related eGRC technology and information systems to support the enhancement of the Fund's risk framework and develop additional tools for identifying and analyzing risks.


Major Duties and Responsibilities


The successful candidate will provide coverage for designated operational risk areas and deliver specific analytical, risk assessments, risk reporting, and data-management responsibilities assigned for the duration of the appointment.

Specific responsibilities include:

  • Examine and evaluate issues in the Fund's strategic, core, and cross-functional risk areas using qualitative and quantitative economic and statistical methods, techniques, and institutional knowledge of the Fund; communicate risks, priorities, and necessary remediation actions effectively.
  • Maintain and enhance departmental models for assessing risks, including risks related to lending, budget, and information security.
  • Analyze the Fund-wide incident reporting database using operational risk methods and statistical modeling to interpret and predict potential risks.
  • Participate in the review and analytical work on the Fund@Risk survey.
  • Process, consolidate, and transform datasets within and between databases using statistical and/or econometric techniques.
  • Draft sections of analytical papers and Board documents prepared by ORM, and review and comment on documents, memoranda, and reports related to cross-functional risk management.
  • Prepare charts, tables, and presentations to support risk reporting and other communications.
  • Collaborate with departments and remain current on academic research concerning emerging risk topics.


Minimum Qualifications


Educational development, typically acquired by the completion of an advanced university degree, or equivalent, in business, accounting, economics, finance, information technology, law, communications, organizational development, or a related field, or a professional certification either as an Accountant (CPA or international equivalent) or as an Auditor (CIA or CISA), supplemented by a minimum of four (4) years of relevant work experience, is required. Alternatively, a minimum of two (2) years of experience in a related position at Grade A10, or equivalent, is required.

The ideal candidate will also possess the following:

  • Experience with data extraction and analytical tools such as Python, VBA, or SQL.
  • Proficiency with presentation and visualization software, such as Keynote, PowerPoint, Adobe Creative Suite, and Tableau.
  • Previous experience in risk assessment and exposure to Fund policies and organizational procedures, including experience in area and/or functional departments. Strong knowledge of Fund procedures is required.
  • Proficiency with external IMF economic and emerging risk databases, including Bloomberg, OECD, and other global risk databases.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate with others, initiate action plans, manage change, make impactful decisions, and complete challenging assignments.
  • Exceptional technical and analytical skills, including experience with Microsoft Excel and preparing presentations.
  • Ability to quickly understand systems, situations, pressures, and the Fund's culture to identify potential risks and determine how best to achieve business goals in the face of those obstacles.
  • Strong oral and written communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical ideas to nontechnical stakeholders and colleagues.
  • Ability to address business challenges consistently and effectively through collaboration and transparency.
  • Demonstrated ability to quickly assimilate technical and institutional context, assume responsibility for an existing work program, and deliver high-quality outputs within a defined assignment period.

This is a one-year contractual appointment. Contractual appointments at the IMF are renewable for up to four years of cumulative contractual service, subject to continued temporary business needs, satisfactory performance, and budget availability.

title: Sr. Long-Range Forecasting & Capacity Planning Analyst
description:
Comcast Business offers a suite of Connectivity, Communications, Networking, Cybersecurity, Wireless, and Managed Solutions to help global organizations of all sizes prepare for what’s next. Powered by the nation’s largest Gig-speed broadband network and backed by 24/7 customer support, Comcast Business is the nation’s largest technology provider to small businesses and one of the leading service providers to the Enterprise market. Comcast Business has been consistently recognized by industry analysts and associations as a leader and innovator, and one of the fastest growing providers of Ethernet services.

Job Summary

The Senior Long-Range Forecasting & Capacity Planning Analyst is responsible for developing long-term staffing, capacity, and financial plans for operations driven primarily by projects, tickets, cases, and other non-call workloads.
This role partners with Operations, Finance, and business leaders to forecast demand, determine staffing requirements, support budgeting, evaluate new initiatives, and quantify productivity and cost-saving opportunities. Because traditional forecasting tools do not support many of these workloads, this role will also be responsible for developing and maintaining custom forecast and staffing models.
Success in this role requires more than producing a forecast. The individual must understand the business drivers behind the forecast, translate those drivers into financial and operational impacts, and provide clear recommendations on the actions the business should take.

Job Description

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and maintain custom forecasting, staffing, and capacity models for project-, ticket-, case-, and other non-call workloads.
  • Translate workload forecasts into staffing requirements using productivity, utilization, shrinkage, and other operational assumptions.
  • Support annual budgeting, monthly finance reviews, and workforce-related financial planning.
  • Analyze actual performance against forecast and budget and explain key staffing and expense variances.
  • Assess staffing and financial impacts of new products, initiatives, projects, or business changes.
  • Build business cases to quantify headcount needs, labor savings, cost avoidance, productivity gains, and ROI.
  • Track whether initiatives deliver expected staffing or financial benefits.
  • Use analytics to identify risks, capacity opportunities, and process improvements.
  • Partner with business leaders to understand future demand and provide clear staffing and financial recommendations.
  • Lead improvements to forecasting and capacity-planning processes, tools, and methodologies.
  • Mentor analysts and provide guidance on forecasting, financial modeling, and business analysis.
  • Consistent exercise of independent judgment and discretion in matters of significance.
  • Regular, consistent and punctual attendance. Must be able to work nights and weekends, variable schedule(s) as necessary.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in workforce planning, forecasting, capacity planning, finance, or operations analytics.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop forecasting and staffing models when established tools or methodologies are not available.
  • Experience developing long-range staffing and capacity models.
  • Experience forecasting non-call workloads such as tickets, projects, cases, or back-office work.
  • Strong financial modeling and budgeting experience.
  • Ability to evaluate staffing requirements and quantify savings from business initiatives.
  • Advanced Excel skills; Power BI, Tableau, SQL, or similar tools preferred.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and business partnership skills.
  • Ability to present complex findings and recommendations to leadership.

Employees at all levels are expected to:

  • Understand our Operating Principles; make them the guidelines for how you do your job.
  • Own the customer experience think and act in ways that put our customers first, give them seamless digital options at every touchpoint, and make them promoters of our products and services.
  • Know your stuff be enthusiastic learners, users and advocates of our game-changing technology, products and services, especially our digital tools and experiences.
  • Win as a team make big things happen by working together and being open to new ideas.
  • Be an active part of the Net Promoter System a way of working that brings more employee and customer feedback into the company by joining huddles, making call backs and helping us elevate opportunities to do better for our customers.
  • Drive results and growth.
  • Support a culture of inclusion in how you work and lead.
  • Do what's right for each other, our customers, investors and our communities.

Job Description:

We are GDIT. The people supporting and securing some of the most complex government, defense,

and intelligence projects across the country. We ensure today is safe and tomorrow is smarter. Our work has meaning and impact on the world around us, but also on us, and that’s important.

GDIT is your place. You make it your own by embracing autonomy, seizing opportunity, and being rusted to deliver your best every day.

We think. We act. We deliver. There is no challenge we can’t turn into opportunity. And our work depends on an Data Science Advisor joining our team to support customer activities.

The Data Science Advisor (DSA) leads the POTFF Enterprise Data and Analytics function and serves as the primary analytical advisor to the Enterprise POTFF Director, Domain Leads, and the Human Factors Council (HFC) on research methodologies, data collection strategies, and program evaluation. The DSA coordinates and directs the technical work of the Data Engineers, Data Scientists, and Senior Data Scientists under their purview, subject to Government direction; sets the analytical agenda in response to Government priorities; ensures that methods are sound, reproducible, and defensible; and delivers findings to Government leadership in a form suitable for decision-making.

HOW A DATA SCIENCE ADVISOR (DSA) WILL MAKE AN IMPACT:


  • Serve as the lead for the Enterprise Data and Analytics function: plan, prioritize, assign, and review the work of the Data Engineers, Data Scientists, and Senior Data Scientists under their purview in response to Government-directed requirements, and manage the analytical backlog using an Agile or comparable framework.
  • Serve as the primary analytical advisor to the Enterprise POTFF Director, Domain Leads, and the HFC regarding research methodologies, data collection strategies, study design, and program evaluation.
  • Design and oversee Government-directed program evaluations, analyses, and experiments that measure the validity, efficacy, and Return on Investment (ROI) of POTFF interventions; select appropriate statistical models and study designs; and ensure data quality and defensible, reproducible methodology.
  • Establish and maintain the team’s analytical standards, data governance practices, reporting methodologies, and performance-measurement frameworks in coordination with Government data governance, and ensure compliance with DoW Impact Level 5 (IL5), HIPAA, Privacy Act, and applicable DoW artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) policy.
  • Translate Government priorities into analytical requirements; support the strategic planning process for POTFF programs with data-driven decision support; and support the development of enterprise performance measures, executive dashboards, and readiness metrics.
  • Prepare and deliver reports, briefings, and decision-support products that accurately convey findings, limitations, and recommendations to Government leadership.
  • Provide consultation to supported units and POTFF staff on opportunities and methods for capturing data on POTFF programs and initiatives, and on the interpretation of analytical products.
  • Coordinate with the USSOCOM Enterprise Data Team and other Government data organizations on data access, standards, and shared platforms, as directed by the Government.
  • Perform advanced analysis personally when required, and maintain currency in statistical analysis, data science, AI/ML, data engineering, and visualization technologies.
  • Coordinate and advise on the training and professional development of the data science personnel under their purview, subject to Government approval.



WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED:


EDUCATION: Master’s degree in a quantitative discipline, including but not limited to statistics, biostatistics, mathematics, applied mathematics, data science, operations research, computer science, engineering, physics, economics or econometrics, epidemiology, geospatial science or geoinformatics, or psychology or another behavioral science with a quantitative-methods concentration, with documented coursework or professional application in statistics, programming, and quantitative analysis; or a bachelor’s degree in such a discipline with the additional experience stated under Required Minimum Experience/Skills below.


  • With a Master’s degree: minimum of seven (7) years of professional experience applying data science, statistics, or research methods to real-world problems, including at least two (2) years supervising or leading analysts. With a bachelor’s degree: minimum of ten (10) years of such experience, including at least two (2) years supervising or leading analysts. In either path, at least three (3) years must be hands-on practice as a data scientist, statistician, or equivalent analyst personally performing the analyses, rather than supervising or advising. Degree-program work does not count toward the Data Science Advisor experience requirement.
  • Demonstrated expertise in research methods, study design, and program evaluation, including quantitative and qualitative methods, sufficient to design defensible evaluations and to advise senior leaders on their limitations.
  • Advanced proficiency in Python or R and in SQL, and demonstrated experience delivering statistical or predictive models and decision-support products to organizational leadership.
  • Demonstrated supervisory experience leading a data science, analytics, or research team, and experience running a program or project of comparable scope.
  • Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing with senior leadership, negotiate complex issues, develop a range of alternatives when there is no single solution, and establish and maintain good working relations with stakeholders.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:


  • Desired (not required): Experience with human performance, sports science, health, clinical, or biomedical data or research.
  • Desired (not required): Agile or Scrum certification (e.g., Certified ScrumMaster, PMI Agile Certified Practitioner) or comparable training.
  • Desired (not required): A doctoral degree in one of the disciplines listed above, or a history of peer-reviewed publications.
  • Desired (not required): Familiarity with the Government-furnished technology stack (e.g., Databricks and Apache Spark, Power BI, Microsoft Power Platform) and with Palantir Foundry.

LOCATION: Various CONUS SITES
