title: SPZ - Space Navigation Engineer
description:
Job Description:

Leonardo è un gruppo industriale internazionale che realizza capacità tecnologiche multidominio per la sicurezza globale. Protagonista dei principali programmi strategici dell’Aerospazio, Difesa e Sicurezza, conta oltre 62.000 dipendenti nel mondo. L’azienda ha una significativa presenza industriale in Italia, Regno Unito, Polonia e Stati Uniti e opera in 150 Paesi anche attraverso controllate, joint venture e partecipazioni. Leonardo è partner tecnologico e industriale di Governi, Amministrazioni della Difesa, Istituzioni e imprese


All’interno della Divisione Spazio, stiamo ricercando un/a Space Navigation Engineer per la nostra sede di Roma - via Faustiniana


La persona si occuperà di:


  • Progettare, sviluppare, implementare e validare algoritmi di navigazione avanzata per sistemi autonomi.
  • Condurre attività di ricerca su tecniche innovative di Artificial Intelligence applicate a Earth Observation, Space Navigation, Exploration e Surveillance, incluse percezione, mapping e motion planning.
  • Studiare e sviluppare tecniche di robust navigation, interference monitoring e mitigazione delle cyber-attacks basate su advanced signal processing e Controlled Radiated Pattern Antenna (CRPA).
  • Analizzare e integrare dati provenienti da sensori eterogenei per migliorare la precisione e la resilienza della navigazione.
  • Prototipare e testare soluzioni di navigazione in ambienti simulati e reali, definendo metriche di performance, procedure di test e criteri di validazione.
  • Collaborare con team di sviluppo software, hardware e AI per integrare algoritmi e moduli di navigazione in piattaforme esistenti.
  • Ottimizzare algoritmi per l’esecuzione real‑time su architetture eterogenee.
  • Documentare risultati, metodologie e processi attraverso report tecnici, documentazione di progetto, pubblicazioni scientifiche e materiali per conferenze.
  • Monitorare lo stato dell’arte tecnico e scientifico, proponendo soluzioni innovative e contribuendo allo sviluppo di nuove metodologie.
  • Contribuire alla definizione delle roadmap tecnologiche relative ai sistemi spaziali autonomi e alle attività di ricerca e sviluppo.
  • Supportare la preparazione di proposte, la pianificazione di progetti, la definizione dei piani di lavoro e la stima delle risorse.
  • Monitorare l’avanzamento tecnico dei progetti rispetto agli obiettivi, fornendo inputs per le review, identificando scostamenti, criticità e rischi.
  • Verificare la conformità delle attività e delle spese rispetto alle linee guida interne e ai requisiti progettuali.
  • Garantire un flusso informativo costante con partner di progetto e funzioni aziendali coinvolte nei rapporti con l’autorità di gestione/ente erogatore.

Titolo di studio:


  • Laurea in discipline STEM (Ingegneria Elettronica, delle Telecomunicazioni o affini).

Livello di esperienza richiesto:


  • Junior/Expert: 1-5 y di esperienzia nel ruolo e/o funzioni analoghe

Competenze e conoscenze tecniche:


  • Fondamenti di navigazione spaziale e terrestre: meccanica orbitale, dinamiche di volo, sistemi di riferimento e trasformazioni.
  • Tecniche di elaborazione del segnale applicate alla navigazione.
  • Sensor fusion: Kalman Filter e varianti (EKF, UKF), Particle Filter, metodi bayesiani.
  • Tecniche di AI per applicazioni spaziali: deep learning, machine learning, federated learning, probabilistic navigation, SLAM, perception & mapping.
  • Architetture e protocolli dei sistemi di posizionamento GNSS (GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou).
  • Modelli fisici e geometrici per navigazione e percezione (camera models, LiDAR models, error budgeting).
  • Principi di integrity e cyber‑resilience per sistemi di navigazione: RAIM, A‑RAIM, interference monitoring, anomaly detection, robust algorithm design, sensor threat mitigation.
  • Sviluppo software per sistemi embedded e real‑time, con ottimizzazione su CPU, GPU ed edge computing.
  • Conoscenza degli standard e normative del settore spazio (ECSS, ESA, NASA) relativi a sviluppo software, qualifica e documentazione.
  • Capacità di redigere documentazione tecnica, report, deliverable e pubblicazioni scientifiche.
  • Costituisce un plus l’esperienza maturata in ambito Spazio in aziende, centri di ricerca o consorzi internazionali.

Competenze comportamentali:


  • Orientamento ai risultati
  • Team work
  • Negoziazione
  • Comunicazione efficace
  • Orientamento al cliente
  • Problem Solving
  • Flessibilità
  • Organizzazione e Pianificazione

Conoscenze linguistiche:


  • Inglese (liv. min. B2)

Competenze informatiche:


  • Framework e tool di simulazione: MATLAB/Simulink, ANSYS STK.
  • Python (NumPy, SciPy, TensorFlow/PyTorch, OpenCV)
  • C and C/C++

Altro:


  • Disponibilità a trasferte in Italia e all’estero.

title: Security Operations Supervisor
description:
Our vision aims to empower our clients by actively leveraging our broad range of services. With our global presence, we have career opportunities all across the world which can lead to a unique, exciting and fulfilling career path. Pick your path today! To see what career opportunities we have available, explore below to find your next career!

We will never request sensitive information such as Social Security numbers or bank details during the initial stages of the recruitment process. If you suspect fraudulent activity, contact us directly through our official channels. Stay safe and protect your personal information.



Location: Rmelan, Hasakah Governorate, Northeast Syria


Job Summary

The Security Operations Supervisor is responsible for the direct operational supervision, coordination, inspection, and performance management of a large-scale security workforce supporting HKN's oil and gas operations throughout Northeast Syria.


The position provides field-level leadership and oversight of static security operations across oil production facilities, well sites, gas processing facilities, checkpoints, access control points, and other designated HKN locations. The Supervisor ensures that all security personnel, including locally employed subcontractor personnel, perform their assigned duties in accordance with HKN requirements, approved post orders, security procedures, applicable laws, and Consortium operating standards.


The successful candidate must possess extensive experience managing large, geographically dispersed security forces in complex or high-risk environments, preferably supporting oil and gas or other critical infrastructure operations. The position requires a hands-on leader capable of supervising local security personnel, enforcing operational discipline, conducting inspections, resolving performance deficiencies, and maintaining effective working relationships with HKN management, local authorities, and community representatives.

The Security Operations Supervisor is expected to spend significant time conducting field inspections and supervising security operations rather than performing duties exclusively from the Operations Support Centre.


Duties and Responsibilities

  • Provide direct operational oversight of the security force assigned to HKN facilities and operational locations throughout Northeast Syria. The current contract scope includes 539 Access Control Manpower positions distributed across Quick Reaction Force operations, material escorts, checkpoints, well security, the gas plant, Tal Adas, Sazaba, violations follow-up, and watchkeeping functions.
  • Ensure all security positions are staffed by appropriately vetted, trained, qualified, and authorized personnel in accordance with approved staffing schedules and operational requirements.
  • Supervise local security subcontractor managers, site supervisors, shift leaders, and guards to ensure consistent implementation of approved security procedures and performance standards.
  • Conduct routine and unannounced inspections of security posts, including night shifts, remote facilities, and high-risk operational locations. Inspections will evaluate personnel accountability, alertness, professional conduct, weapons safety, equipment condition, communications, post documentation, and compliance with established procedures.
  • Identify operational deficiencies and initiate immediate corrective measures when necessary to protect HKN personnel, facilities, and operations.
  • Coordinate with the Security Operations Manager and subcontractor leadership to develop and maintain operational staffing plans, duty rosters, shift assignments, relief coverage, and contingency staffing arrangements.
  • Verify personnel attendance and post coverage through regular review of staffing reports, attendance records, supervisory inspections, and information received from the Operations Support Centre.
  • Ensure appropriate personnel are available to address absences, illness, emergency leave, training requirements, and unexpected staffing shortages without compromising required security coverage.
  • Monitor shift patterns, fatigue, and workforce welfare to support compliance with applicable labor requirements and HKN operational standards.
  • Coordinate security staffing adjustments resulting from changing operational requirements, emerging threats, facility activities, and HKN-directed priorities.
  • Oversee implementation and enforcement of site-specific security plans, post orders, access control procedures, and physical security measures at HKN facilities.
  • Ensure security personnel properly verify identification and access authorization, control vehicle and pedestrian entry, maintain visitor and material movement records, and implement established search and inspection procedures.
  • Conduct periodic physical security assessments to identify vulnerabilities involving perimeter protection, access points, lighting, barriers, surveillance equipment, guard placement, and security procedures.
  • Coordinate with HKN facility representatives to address security concerns affecting production facilities, personnel accommodations, equipment, materials, and other critical assets.
  • Ensure security personnel understand the importance of protecting oil and gas operations while minimizing unnecessary interference with authorized production, maintenance, and logistics activities.
  • Serve as a principal field-level representative responsible for monitoring the operational performance of local security subcontractors.
  • Evaluate subcontractor compliance with contractual staffing requirements, personnel qualifications, post orders, training standards, equipment accountability, and HKN security expectations.
  • Conduct documented inspections and performance assessments, identify deficiencies, and coordinate corrective action plans with subcontractor management.
  • Monitor the effectiveness of subcontractor supervisors and shift leaders, ensuring they exercise appropriate leadership, maintain discipline, and address performance problems promptly.
  • Recommend retraining, reassignment, disciplinary action, or removal of personnel who fail to meet established security requirements, in accordance with Consortium procedures and applicable employment arrangements.
  • Support the Security Operations Manager in evaluating subcontractor performance and maintaining accountability for security services delivered under the contract.
  • Provide field-level leadership during security incidents, emergencies, disturbances, unauthorized access attempts, security breaches, and other events affecting HKN operations.
  • Coordinate incident response with the Operations Support Centre, Quick Reaction Force personnel, HKN security management, and appropriate local authorities.
  • Ensure security personnel follow approved emergency response procedures, use-of-force requirements, incident notification protocols, and escalation procedures.
  • Respond to significant incidents as directed, assess conditions, coordinate security resources, and provide accurate operational updates to management.
  • Ensure incidents are properly documented, evidence is preserved when appropriate, and reports are submitted within contractual reporting timelines.
  • Participate in incident investigations, after-action reviews, and the development of corrective measures intended to prevent recurrence.
  • Work closely with the Consortium Training Manager to assess the operational proficiency of security personnel and identify individual and collective training requirements.
  • Provide direct mentoring and practical coaching to local security supervisors, team leaders, and guards, emphasizing leadership, professional conduct, operational discipline, communications, access control, incident response, and compliance with post orders.
  • Observe personnel performing their assigned duties and provide constructive feedback to improve operational effectiveness.
  • Assist in implementing practical exercises, emergency drills, post-specific training, and competency assessments.
  • Identify personnel with leadership potential and support their development into senior guard, shift supervisor, site supervisor, and other supervisory positions.
  • Verify that personnel assigned to security duties possess the required training, certifications, and authorizations, and report deficiencies to the Training Manager and Security Operations Manager.
  • Monitor the operational readiness and accountability of Quick Reaction Force personnel assigned within the static security establishment.
  • Ensure QRF personnel are appropriately staffed, equipped, trained, and prepared to respond in accordance with approved response procedures.
  • Coordinate with the Operations Support Centre to confirm QRF availability, communications readiness, and incident response arrangements.
  • Support coordination between static security0 personnel, QRF elements, and Protective Security Detail teams when operations require additional security support.
  • Participate in operational exercises and evaluate the effectiveness of coordination between site security personnel and responding resources.
  • Monitor compliance with approved weapons handling, storage, issuance, and accountability procedures applicable to armed security personnel.
  • Conduct or participate in inspections of weapons, ammunition records, communications equipment, protective equipment, and other security resources.
  • Ensure personnel assigned armed duties possess the appropriate authorization and current weapons qualifications.
  • Identify unserviceable, damaged, missing, or improperly maintained equipment and coordinate corrective action through the appropriate management channels.
  • Verify that security posts maintain reliable communications with the Operations Support Centre and that personnel understand established emergency communications and reporting procedures.
  • Maintain professional working relationships with relevant local security authorities, including Asayish representatives, community leaders, and other authorized stakeholders as directed by Consortium management.
  • Support coordination concerning security personnel authorization, facility access, local security concerns, and incidents involving community members or local authorities.
  • Use cultural awareness and local knowledge to assist in resolving misunderstandings, personnel disputes, and community concerns before they adversely affect HKN operations.
  • Ensure all engagement with authorities and community representatives is conducted professionally, lawfully, and in accordance with HKN and Consortium policies.
  • The Supervisor will not independently make contractual commitments, authorize payments, or negotiate arrangements with government or security authorities without appropriate management authorization.
  • Prepare and submit accurate operational reports covering security inspections, staffing deficiencies, incidents, equipment condition, training observations, and corrective actions.
  • Maintain inspection records and monitor assigned corrective actions through completion.
  • Provide regular operational updates to the Security Operations Manager and participate in management meetings, security assessments, and performance reviews.
  • Support implementation of the project Quality Control Plan and Health, Safety and Environmental Management Plan.
  • Ensure security personnel comply with HKN safety requirements, including appropriate personal protective equipment, safe vehicle operations, fatigue management, heat stress prevention, and site-specific hazards associated with oil and gas facilities.
  • Exercise stop-work or stop-activity authority when an immediate threat to personnel safety exists, consistent with approved procedures.

Qualifications

  • A minimum of eight years of progressively responsible experience in security operations, military security, law enforcement, critical infrastructure protection, or a closely related field is required.
  • At least five years of demonstrated supervisory or management experience overseeing security personnel, including experience managing multiple sites, shift operations, and geographically dispersed security teams.
  • Demonstrated experience supervising large security workforces, preferably involving 100 or more personnel, with responsibility for staffing accountability, operational inspections, performance management, and incident response.
  • Prior experience supporting oil and gas production facilities, energy infrastructure, industrial installations, or similarly complex critical infrastructure is strongly preferred.
  • Experience operating in Northeast Syria, the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, or comparable high-risk environments is highly desirable. Direct familiarity with Hasakah Governorate, Rmelan, Qamishli, and surrounding operating areas is preferred.
  • Prior military or law enforcement supervisory experience is desirable but is not a substitute for demonstrated large-scale security management capability.
  • Must be proficient in spoken and written English, including the ability to communicate with expatriate management, prepare operational reports, conduct briefings, and understand written security procedures. Must be fluent in spoken Kurdish, preferably the Kurmanji dialect used in Northeast Syria, and capable of effectively supervising and communicating with local security personnel. Language proficiency will be assessed during the interview and selection process.
  • The successful candidate must demonstrate sound knowledge of static security operations, access control, physical security inspections, security workforce management, emergency response coordination, incident reporting, and operational risk assessment.
  • Candidates must possess practical knowledge of security post orders, guard force supervision, weapons safety and accountability, communications procedures, and the management of security personnel operating in high-risk environments.
  • Experience working with security operations centers, electronic reporting systems, GPS tracking platforms, and Microsoft Office applications is required or must be demonstrated through equivalent operational systems experience.
  • The candidate must be capable of preparing professional written reports, maintaining accurate operational records, and communicating clearly with both local personnel and senior management.

Acuity International is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, national origin, age, disability, or protected veteran status.

Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure safe transport of food, lifesaving medicines and more. The Digital Technology Leadership Program (DTLP) is a two-year leadership development program designed to prepare high-potential college graduates to become future leaders within Carrier’s Digital Technology organization.

Through three eight-month rotations across Carrier’s Digital organization, you will gain broad, hands-on experience while building the leadership, business, and technical skills needed to lead teams, manage products, solve complex challenges, and deliver meaningful results. description:
Job Title

Senior Director of Operations & Supply Chain (CPG)

Job Description

About the Position | Major goals and objectives and location requirements:

We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on Senior Operations Director to build and lead end-to-end operations for a new CPG beverage brand. You will own the physical life cycle of the product—from commercialization and sourcing through production, inventory, warehousing, shipping, and replenishment. You’ll work closely with Sales, Marketing, Finance, and manufacturing partners to ensure we make the right product, at the right quality and cost, and get it where it needs to go on time. This is a role for a builder and operator—someone who can create scalable systems and partnerships while staying close enough to production and supply chain execution to solve problems quickly.


What You’ll Do

  • Own end-to-end operations from commercialization through production, customer delivery and replenishment.
  • Build the supply chain, vendor network and operating processes required to launch and scale the business.
  • Translate forecasts into production, inventory and supply plans, including co-manufacturer capacity, scheduling and production readiness.
  • Manage sourcing and external partners across ingredients, packaging, co-manufacturers, warehouses, 3PLs and freight.
  • Work closely with the VP/GM on the commercialization of new products and formats across formula, packaging, specifications and production requirements.
  • Partner with quality, regulatory and technical resources on food safety, process authority and compliance.
  • Own inventory, warehousing, fulfillment and transportation across retail, distributor, foodservice and DTC channels.
  • Own key components of COGS and landed cost, while managing operational KPIs across production, inventory, service, freight and cost.

  • 10+ years of operations, supply chain or manufacturing experience, including at least 7 years in beverage.
  • Direct beverage manufacturing experience required, ideally in RTD, non-alcoholic beverages, beer, wine, or spirits utilizing glass and aluminum packaging.
  • Experience managing products from commercialization through production, distribution, and replenishment.
  • Strong experience with co-manufacturers/co-packers, outsourced manufacturing and external supply-chain partners.
  • Deep knowledge of production planning, sourcing, ingredients and packaging, inventory, warehousing and transportation.
  • Strong financial and operational judgment, including COGS, landed cost, budgets, working capital, vendor negotiation and project management.

title: Payments Risk & Resilience Lead Business Analyst - Assistant Vice President
description:
Who we are looking for:

We are looking for an experienced payments resilience and business-change lead to coordinate the business readiness, requirements and operating-model implications of SWIFT resiliency capabilities and other contingency related programs. The role will work closely with the anomaly detection and traceability leads so that infrastructure resilience, transaction visibility, controls, testing and operational response are designed as one coherent capability.


Why this role is important to us?

Our Payments Business Risk and Resiliency Programs includes strategic resilience planning for SWIFT cold-start failover and alternative-network capabilities. Effective adoption requires clear business requirements, governance decisions, operating procedures, test plans and global readiness across payment operations and supporting technology teams.

Join us if contributing to our Payments Business Risk and Resiliency Programs is a challenge you are up for.


What you will be responsible for

  • Lead the business analysis and readiness plan for SWIFT resiliency , aligned to programme milestones, external dependencies and internal governance.
  • Translate SWIFT and architecture inputs into business requirements, operating impacts, decisions, risks, assumptions and implementation action.
  • Map critical payment and settlement flows, applications, infrastructure dependencies, identities, connectivity, monitoring points and recovery requirements.
  • Coordinate decisions on usage model, operating model, governance, global adoption, pilot scope, capabilities, controls and escalation routes.
  • Develop readiness criteria, playbooks, business continuity procedures, recovery roles and alternative-processing scenarios.
  • Partner with Technology, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Resiliency and Operations on design reviews, control requirements and evidence needs.
  • Define and coordinate tabletop exercises, connectivity tests, failover simulations, pilot preparation and business acceptance activities.
  • Use the traceability workstream’s application maps and event data to define transaction monitoring and evidence requirements during disruption and recovery.
  • Align anomaly detection and cyber-response processes so suspicious or incorrect payment activity is triaged effectively during resilience events.
  • Prepare steering updates, decision papers, risk assessments and post-test remediation plans; support transition to ongoing BAU resilience governance.

What we value:

These skills will help you succeed in this role:

  • Strong knowledge of global payments, SWIFT messaging infrastructure and operational resilience or business continuity.
  • Experience translating technical architecture or external-industry initiatives into business requirements and readiness plans.
  • Strong process, dependency, risk and control analysis skills.
  • Experience designing or coordinating resilience tests, pilots, failover exercises or production-readiness activity.
  • Ability to influence senior stakeholders across Operations, Technology, Cybersecurity and Risk.

Education & Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, technology, risk or a related discipline.
  • 7+ years of relevant financial services experience, including payments and resilience, infrastructure or major change.
  • Business continuity, operational resilience, SWIFT or project-delivery qualifications are advantageous.

About State Street

What we do. State Street is one of the largest custodian banks, asset managers and asset intelligence companies in the world. From technology to product innovation, we make our mark on the financial services industry. description:
Who we are looking for:

We are looking for a senior payments business analyst to lead the design and implementation of an enterprise end-to-end payment and settlement traceability capability. The role will map payment journeys across applications, define lifecycle events and exception states, shape the target operating model, while also supporting the anomaly detection and Swift Resilience workstreams where traceability, event data and process knowledge are shared dependencies.


Why this role is important to us?

Payment status information is currently distributed across origination, middleware, screening, credit, repair, market gateway and reconciliation platforms. A unified traceability capability will support faster incident triage, improved client communication, operational resilience and audit-ready evidence.

Join us if contributing to our Payments Business Risk and Resiliency Programs is a challenge you are up for.


What you will be responsible for

  • Lead discovery and business analysis across in-scope payment and settlement applications, rails, gateways and operating teams.
  • Create and maintain the application inventory, end-to-end process maps, lifecycle-event model, exception taxonomy, data lineage and ownership model.
  • Define requirements for payment search, identifier correlation, real-time or near-real-time status, lifecycle drill-down, ACK/NACK visibility, alerts, reporting and evidence export.

  • Support Swift resilience work where required

These skills will help you succeed in this role:

  • Deep knowledge of end-to-end payment processing and the interaction between origination, middleware, screening, credit, repair, gateways and markets.
  • Strong business analysis, process mapping, data lineage and requirements-management capability.
  • Experience with payment identifiers, SWIFT or ISO 20022 messaging, ACK/NACK statuses and operational exception handling.

Job Description

The Malnutrition Informatics Specialist RD will focus on malnutrition to lead and manage our organization's malnutrition program. This job requires a deep understanding of malnutrition program development and implementation from both a clinical nutrition and data-driven perspective. This position will focus on the accuracy of patient identification, nutrition interventions, physician diagnosis, and billing process to show continuous quality improvement. It will also mentor, train, and provide continual support to the hospital RDs and Clinical Nutrition Managers (CNMs) within the assigned region. The Malnutrition Informatics Specialist RD will analyze program data, track key performance indicators (KPIs), and provide education training to healthcare teams to drive patient outcomes and enhance the overall impact of malnutrition.

Responsibilities

Join the Nouri Team at HHS, LLC as a Malnutrition Specialist


Starting salary $75,000 (Negotiable based on experience)


Travel: Up to 75% travel; close proximity to a major airport preferred


Malnutrition Program Management

  • Oversee the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the hospital's malnutrition programs in assigned area.
  • Track KPIs to assess the effectiveness of the malnutrition program in improving patient outcomes and increasing malnutrition recognition.
  • Analyze monthly hospital site-specific data.
  • Utilize data analytics to monitor trends in malnutrition diagnoses, interventions, and outcomes, and make data-driven recommendations for program adjustments.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with physicians, nursing staff, RDs, and other healthcare professionals to foster a collaborative approach to malnutrition management.
  • Lead or participate in multidisciplinary committees, meetings, and training sessions to raise awareness about malnutrition and ensure best practices in screening, diagnosis, and treatment. Ensure staff are knowledgeable about current malnutrition-related guidelines, tools, and evidence-based practices.

Clinical Support

  • Conduct ongoing monitoring and training on malnutrition assessment and documentation for RDs and CNMs, ensuring efficiency and effectiveness of malnutrition program.
  • Assist RDs and facilities to achieve a quality standard of care, adhering to ASPEN guidelines when screening and assessing for malnutrition.
  • Assist Regional Director of Clinical Nutrition with monitoring RDs clinical competency for regulatory compliance.
  • Provide clinical coverage in areas of responsibility as needed that includes completing documentation of nutrition assessments/follow-ups for patients at risk of malnutrition.
  • Adhere to all HHS policies and procedures.
  • Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability in rapidly integrating into diverse team and clinical environments that may include varied electronic medical records, workflows, and clinical protocols.

Quality Assurance

  • Regularly assess program performance and impact through data collection, audits, and performance reviews.
  • Provide reports to HHS leadership on program outcomes, including trends in malnutrition rates, identification accuracy, and overall impact on patient care and revenue.
  • Identify opportunities for improvement based on data trends and feedback from clinical teams.
  • Advocate for organizational policies and clinical practices that promote early recognition, accurate diagnosis, and appropriate treatment of malnutrition.

Job Specifications

  • Registered Dietitian with Commission on Dietetic Registration and a Licensed Dietitian as required per state regulations.
  • 5 or more years of work experience in a related clinical role is required.
  • Expert knowledge of malnutrition, including Nutrition Focused Physical Exam (NFPE) per ASPEN guidelines.
  • Conduct self in a positive, professional manner.
  • Self-starter, able to work independently.
  • Experience in data collection and analysis using Excel spreadsheets and proficiency in computer skills.
  • Multi-task, manage personnel remotely, able to travel up to 75% of their time (both air and ground).
  • Communicate effectively with clients, customers, management teams, and clinical teams, both orally and in writing

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate in High-Dimensional Quantum Photonics
description:
Role Title: Postdoctoral Research Associate in High-Dimensional Quantum Photonics

Grade and Salary: Grade 7 - £38,448 - £48,337 per annum

FTE and working pattern: Full-time (35hrs per week) Fixed Term for 12 months

Reward and Benefits: 33 days annual leave, plus 9 buildings closed days for all full-time staff.

Detailed Description

This is 1-year postdoctoral position in the Beyond Binary Quantum Information research group led by Prof Mehul Malik at the Institute of Photonics and Quantum Sciences (IPAQS) at Heriot-Watt University in Edinburgh, Scotland. In this role, you will be involved in cutting-edge research projects focusing on the study of high-dimensional quantum states of light encoded in time. Your research will aim at gaining exquisite control over the temporal structure of quantum light, with the ultimate goal of advancing next-generation quantum technologies for communication and computing. You will play an integral role in ongoing BBQLab projects as well as in the planning and delivery of upcoming research projects.

This is a role with a significant amount of responsibility. It will involve overseeing all aspects of our group’s research—from supervising the activities of junior group members, to contributing to the planning and writing of external grant proposals. There is plenty of flexibility for pursuing your own research agenda as long as it is aligned with lab activities. You will have a strong support network for the development your own career through independent grant/fellowship applications. A willingness and ability to travel globally would be an advantage.

For examples of our recent research, please see our group’s publications page:

Key Duties and Responsibilities

We are looking for a creative and driven researcher who is extremely passionate about research. You should hold (or have submitted) a PhD in Quantum Information Science, Quantum Engineering or a related field, and have experience planning and leading experiments within an experimental photonics lab. A solid background in theoretical quantum information science and experimental experience with quantum photonics is essential. In addition to the above, the candidate will be expected to:

  • Conduct individual and collaborative research projects while making use of relevant research techniques and methods. Use initiative and creativity to identify exciting directions for research, develop new research methods, and extend the research portfolio.
  • Supervise the activities of junior group members and PhD students, while assisting in the development of student knowledge and research skills. Ensure continuity of experimental techniques and methodology developed in the group.
  • Disseminate results of research through high-quality publications in peer-reviewed journals and conference presentations. Significant financial support is available for attending national and international conferences.
  • Contribute to the planning of research projects and in the preparation of proposals and applications to external bodies, e.g. for funding purposes. Support will also be provided to the researcher for developing independent applications for grants/fellowships from national/international funding bodies.
  • Make and develop internal and external contacts with a view towards knowledge-sharing and building relationships for collaborative research.
  • Assist in the day-to-day maintenance of the experimental facilities and liaise with companies. A working knowledge of lasers, spatial light modulators, optical fibres and/or cryogenic photodetectors is desirable.
  • The successful candidate is also expected to be involved in our outreach activities, with roles that can be tuned to the specific preferences of the candidate but will involve for example interviews, talks for the general public, and preparation of experimental demonstrators.

Education, Qualifications and Experience

Essential

  1. Applicants should hold a PhD (or a thesis submitted by the start date of the project) in quantum information science, quantum engineering, or a related field
  2. A record of high quality, peer-reviewed publications and evidence of contribution to the writing of these publications proportionate to opportunity.
  3. Experimental experience with time-bin quantum states of light, complex scattering media, and photonic spatial modes.
  4. Strong theoretical understanding and thorough grounding in quantum information science.
  5. Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  6. Experience planning and leading experiments within an experimental lab.
  7. Experience of programming for data acquisition and analysis (e.g. MATLAB, Python).
  8. Experience in public presentation of scientific results, e.g. contributed talks at conferences.
  9. Ability to work on one's own initiative.
  10. Must be able to work as part of the BBQ Lab team and more widely with collaborators at other Universities.

Desirable

  1. Creative approach to research.
  2. Strong people management skills.
  3. Experience of research student supervision.
  4. Experience in leading the writing of scientific papers.

About our Team

The Beyond Binary Quantum Information research group is a dynamic team of researchers working at the interface of quantum information theory and experiment, with a specific focus on exploring high-dimensional quantum photonic systems. We are developing methods to generate, manipulate, and measure complex quantum states of light encoded in the spatial and temporal degrees-of-freedom and applying them in fundamental tests of quantum mechanics for enhancing modern quantum technologies for communication, sensing, and computing.

The BBQ Lab is situated in custom-built, state-of-the-art photonics laboratories outfitted with a wide range of equipment including: femtosecond-pulsed and CW sources of entanglement at telecom and visible wavelengths, superconducting nanowire detectors and arrays, and spatial light modulators (SLMs/DMDs). We are funded by generous grants from UKRI/EPSRC, the European Research Council, and the Royal Academy of Engineering. We are co-leads on two UK National Quantum Technology Hubs (Networks, Sensing and Imaging) and the EPSRC Applied Quantum Technologies Centre for Doctoral Training (CDT). We have substantial resources available for travel and career development and have strong links to leadings research group in the EU and North America.

How to Apply

Please submit via the Heriot-Watt on-line recruitment system (1) Cover letter describing your interest and suitability for the post; (2) Full CV

Applications can be submitted until 23:55 on Wednesday 21 October 2026.

We may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. We therefore encourage you to submit your application promptly.

We recognise that many candidates use AI tools during the application process and are comfortable with AI being used as a supporting aid. However, we want to hear from you, not AI.

Your application should be an authentic representation of your skills, experience and achievements. Applications that appear to have been fully generated by AI may not accurately reflect your suitability for the role and are therefore discouraged.

At interview, candidates will be expected to discuss and provide evidence of the experience, skills and examples included in their application.

About Heriot-Watt University

At Heriot Watt we are passionate about our values and look to them to connect our people globally and to help us collaborate and celebrate our success through working together. Our research programmes can deliver real world impact which is achieved through the diversity of our international community and the recognition of creative talent that connects our global team.

Our flourishing community will give you the freedom to challenge and to bring your enterprising mind and to help our partners with solutions that can be applied now and in the future. Join us and Heriot Watt will provide you with a platform to thrive and work in a way that also helps you live your life in balance with well-being and inclusiveness at the heart of our global community.

Heriot-Watt University is committed to securing equality of opportunity in employment and to the creation of an environment in which individuals are selected, trained, promoted, appraised and otherwise treated on the sole basis of their relevant merits and abilities. Equality and diversity are all about maximising potential and creating a culture of inclusion for all.

Heriot-Watt University values diversity across our University community and welcomes applications from all sectors of society, particularly from underrepresented groups. For more information, please see our website https://www.hw.ac.uk/uk/services/equality-diversity.htm and also our award-winning work in Disability Inclusive Science Careers https://disc.hw.ac.uk/ .

We welcome and will consider flexible working patterns e.g. part-time working and job share options.

Use our total rewards calculator: https://www.hw.ac.uk/about/work/total-rewards-calculator.htm to see the value of benefits provided by Heriot-Watt University.
